question: How would you make a limbless mouse? A cross-scale design-route map.

scales.label: Molecular / sequence
scales.blurb: Change non-coding DNA and leave every protein intact. This is the layer where a limb can be removed without touching anything else the gene does, and it is the layer evolution used in snakes and sticklebacks. It is also the only layer a genome language model emits a score for.

scales.label: Gene / coding
scales.blurb: Delete or break the protein. The phenotypes here are the strongest and best documented, and most of them kill the animal for a reason that has nothing to do with limbs - lung, kidney, allantois, heart. The gene scale tells you what a node does; it rarely gives you an animal.

scales.label: Cell / signalling centre
scales.blurb: Remove or silence the AER or the ZPA as structures, rather than the genes that specify them. This is where the subject started, with a scalpel, and it is where the timing question is posed most directly: cut the ridge off later and you get more limb.

scales.label: Tissue / pattern formation
scales.blurb: The circuits that decide how big the bud gets and how many digits it carries: a self-terminating SHH-GREM1-FGF loop and a BMP-SOX9-WNT Turing system whose wavelength distal Hox dose sets. These explain limb FORM. None of them has been shown to explain limb ABSENCE, and the page says so.

scales.label: Developmental timing
scales.blurb: Apply the lesion when you choose rather than at fertilisation. This is the scale that converts lethal mutants into viable animals and binary genotypes into ordered series, and it is where our recommendation sits. The same Tbx4 deletion gives blocked outgrowth, proximal hypoplasia, or nothing at all, depending only on the hour.

scales.label: Organism / evolutionary comparative
scales.blurb: Four independent natural limb losses - snakes, limb-reduced skinks, cetaceans, stickleback pelvis - solved by at least three different mechanisms at three different layers. They are the ground truth this subject has and ours does not, and they are the reason to present a design space instead of an answer.

scales.label: Non-animal / in vitro
scales.blurb: Budoids, human iPSC limb-bud mesenchyme, limb-bud explants, recombinant limbs and trunk-like structures. The route a modern reviewer asks about first, the route with the best welfare case, and the route whose honest limit is that no dish currently makes a limb.

routes.title: Replace the mouse ZRS with a snake ortholog (king cobra or Burmese python)
routes.mechanism: The ZRS is a limb-specific enhancer of Shh sitting ~1 Mb from the Shh promoter inside Lmbr1 intron 5, and it is the sole driver of Shh expression in the posterior limb bud mesenchyme. Snake ZRS orthologs have accumulated substitutions that destroy the transcription-factor binding sites the enhancer needs, so an otherwise wild-type mouse carrying a snake ZRS makes no limb-bud Shh. Every protein in the genome is left intact; only 1.3 kb of non-coding DNA changes.
routes.intervention: CRISPR/Cas9 homology-directed replacement of the functionally critical 1.3 kb ZRS core with the same-length orthologous sequence from king cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) or Burmese python (Python bivittatus). Kvon et al. did exactly this in FVB mice with a matched-littermate design.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Severe TRUNCATION of both fore- and hindlimbs, not amelia. The cobra knock-in gives complete loss of limb-bud Shh and a phenotype indistinguishable from deleting the enhancer outright; the proximal skeleton is present. The python knock-in is slightly milder: most elements distal to the stylopod:zeugopod junction are severely affected, but 2-3 rudimentary digits form in the forelimb and a slightly enlarged ossification resembling a rudimentary zeugopod appears, attributed to very weak residual Shh transcript detectable only after prolonged in-situ development.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11, 'Progressive Loss of Function in a Limb Enhancer during Snake Evolution'
evidence.finding: Replacing the mouse ZRS with the cobra ortholog 'resulted in a complete loss of [Shh] expression and a truncated limb phenotype, affecting both the fore- and hindlimbs, that is indistinguishable from the phenotype caused by deletion of the mouse enhancer'. The python ortholog gave 'a similar but a slightly milder phenotype ... 2-3 rudimentary digits in the forelimb'. Human and coelacanth orthologs rescued fully developed limbs.

routes.reversibility: Not reversible in the animal: this is a germline sequence change fixed at the zygote. It IS reversible at the design stage - reintroducing 17 bp restores normal limbs (see mol-zrs-e1-ets-site), which makes the allele series itself a dose knob rather than a switch.
routes.lethality_risk: Low. ZRS-null mice are alive and of comparable body size at two weeks of age; Kvon et al. photographed them. Mouse ZRS reporter assays show no reproducible activity outside the limb and ZRS deletion studies report no phenotypes beyond limb defects, so there is no known non-limb organ requirement.
routes.specificity: Limb only, both pairs, posterior-distal. It removes the autopod and zeugopod and spares the stylopod and girdle. It does not touch lung, kidney, allantois, neural tube or craniofacial structures.
routes.difficulty: low-to-medium. The exact sgRNA, donor design, homology arms and genotyping primers are published; the line already exists in at least one lab. Cost is a standard CRISPR knock-in campaign plus a mouse colony.
routes.what_we_would_run: Score the published ortholog series with a genome language model (we have an Evo 2 7B pipeline that has produced one real paired result on zebrafish regulatory windows) and ask whether the model's ranking reproduces the measured ranking: human ~ coelacanth (normal) > python (weak residual) > cobra (none). Pre-register the prediction. Controls: dinucleotide shuffles and GC-matched random windows, as in the run we already did.
open_questions: Does a sequence model separate cobra from coelacanth, given that coelacanth shares LESS sequence identity with human ZRS (57%) than python does (59%) yet behaves like wild type? This is the single sharpest test in the dataset and it is an explicit identity-versus-function dissociation.
Boa ZRS retained ZPA reporter activity but was never taken to knock-in, so the 'ordered series' is four knock-in phenotypes plus reporter data, not a uniform assay.

routes.title: Delete the ZRS outright
routes.mechanism: Removing the enhancer removes the only known driver of limb-bud Shh. Shh protein is still made everywhere else it is normally made (notochord, floor plate, gut), so the animal has no midline, neural-tube or axial defect. This is the cleanest available dissociation between 'Shh the gene' and 'Shh in the limb'.
routes.intervention: CRISPR/Cas9 deletion of the 1,324 bp ZRS (mm10 chr5:29,314,497-29,315,820), or the earlier targeted deletion of the conserved intronic module. Both alleles exist.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Truncation of both limbs with a surviving proximal skeleton. At E18.5 the forelimb humerus, radius and ulna appear fused and no recognisable autopod is present; the hindlimb zeugopod is severely reduced and the autopod is represented by a single rudimentary digit. Animals survive to at least two weeks with body size comparable to wild type.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11
evidence.finding: Figure S3E-F: 'Gross phenotypes of two week old ZRS(+/+) (top) and ZRS(-/-) (bottom) mice. The body sizes are comparable, but ZRS(-/-) mice have truncated limbs.' Skeletal detail as described above.

evidence.cite: Sagai T et al. 2005, Development 132:797-803, 'Elimination of a long-range cis-regulatory module causes complete loss of limb-specific Shh expression and truncation of the mouse limb'
evidence.finding: Targeted deletion of the conserved intronic sequence gives 'a complete loss of Shh expression in the limb bud and degeneration of skeletal elements distal to the stylopod/zygopod junction'.

routes.reversibility: None in the animal. Germline, constitutive.
routes.lethality_risk: Low; this is the only route in the whole design space with a published photograph of a limb-reduced mouse alive at two weeks and of normal body size.
routes.specificity: Limb only, both pairs. Spares girdle and stylopod.
routes.difficulty: low. Two independent alleles published, one of them CRISPR-made specifically to exclude neo-cassette and background effects.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing new computationally - this is the reference phenotype everything else is scored against, and it is the anchor for the honest claim that 'limbless mouse' in the ZRS literature means limb-REDUCED and viable, not amelia.
open_questions: Welfare: a viable animal with truncated limbs is the ethically harder case precisely because it lives. See the welfare section.
No published long-term (adult, >2 week) husbandry or behavioural data was found in our search.

routes.title: Edit the single E1 ETS binding site - a 17 bp switch
routes.mechanism: A 17 bp deletion overlapping the E1 ETS1 recognition motif is the only sequence present in all examined limbed vertebrates and fish and absent from all examined snakes. Reintroducing those 17 bp into an otherwise-python ZRS restores full enhancer activity in the posterior limb-bud mesenchyme and rescues normal limb development in the mouse. Conversely the site is the smallest known handle on the whole system.
routes.intervention: CRISPR knock-in of a 1,341 bp synthetic 'resurrected python' allele (python ZRS plus the 17 bp lizard sequence) in place of the mouse ZRS; or the reciprocal, removing the 17 bp from an otherwise wild-type mouse ZRS.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Reintroduction direction: NORMAL limbs. Removal direction: Kvon et al. state that loss of the E1 motif in the mouse ZRS alone is NOT sufficient to alter limb-bud expression, and boa ZRS is active despite lacking both E0 and E1, so deleting E1 in mouse is predicted to give normal or near-normal limbs. Do not state that removing 17 bp from a mouse removes its limbs; the literature says the opposite.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11
evidence.finding: 'reintroduction of 17 bp of sequence alone was sufficient to reinstate full enhancer activity' and knock-in mice with the modified python allele 'had normal limbs'. Separately: 'the loss of E1 motif in mouse ZRS is not sufficient to alter limb bud expression' and boa ZRS is active despite lacking E0 and E1, so 'loss of these motifs alone cannot explain ZRS deactivation in snake lineage'.

routes.reversibility: This is the one asymmetric, directional result in the design space: the 17 bp is sufficient to RESTORE function on a degraded background but not sufficient to DESTROY function on a healthy one. Context-dependence of this kind is exactly what a per-nucleotide additive sequence model will get wrong.
routes.lethality_risk: None beyond the background allele.
routes.specificity: Limb only.
routes.difficulty: low. Published allele, published sequence.
routes.what_we_would_run: Ask a genome language model for the effect of the 17 bp indel in BOTH directions and on BOTH backgrounds (mouse ZRS minus 17 bp; python ZRS plus 17 bp). A model that reports a symmetric effect has failed a test with a known answer. This is a cheap, pre-registerable, falsifiable experiment, and the published asymmetry means we know the right answer before scoring.
open_questions: Kvon et al. explicitly say ETS-site loss alone cannot explain snake ZRS deactivation and point at homeodomain motifs with a similar snake-specific substitution increase. So E1 is necessary-in-context, not the mechanism.

routes.title: Design a graded ZRS hypomorphic allelic series from the in-vivo variant panel
routes.mechanism: Nearly a thousand human ZRS variants have been assayed in vivo in a high-throughput mouse reporter, and selected variants were confirmed in knock-in mice. That panel is a measured sequence-to-activity map over the exact element that sets limb-bud Shh. In principle one can pick combinations that place enhancer activity at a chosen point between wild type and null and so dial the degree of limb reduction.
routes.intervention: Select variant combinations from the published panel, knock them in, and read out skeletal phenotype at E18.5.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Unknown and the honest answer is that the published panel points the WRONG WAY for this purpose. Kvon et al. 2020 assayed an enhancer 'repeatedly linked to polydactyly' and the knock-in confirmations were of variants that CAUSE polydactyly - a gain of ectopic anterior activity, i.e. extra digits, not fewer. A graded loss-of-function series would have to be designed and tested; it does not exist in that dataset.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2020, Cell 180:1262-1271.e15, 'Comprehensive In Vivo Interrogation Reveals Phenotypic Impact of Human Enhancer Variants'
evidence.finding: '71% of all rare non-coding variants previously proposed as causal lead to reporter gene expression in a pattern consistent with their pathogenic role. Variants observed to alter enhancer activity were further confirmed to cause polydactyly in knockin mice.' Combinatorial and single-nucleotide mutagenesis covered all positions of the enhancer.

evidence.cite: Gurnett CA et al. 2007, Am J Med Genet A 143A:27-32, 'Two novel point mutations in the long-range SHH enhancer in three families with triphalangeal thumb and preaxial polydactyly'
evidence.finding: Point mutations within the ZRS (bp 621, bp 739 of a 774 bp conserved core in LMBR1 intron 5) segregate with triphalangeal thumb and preaxial polydactyly; both alter putative Cdx binding sites. A 5'-end mutation was associated with a milder phenotype and 82% penetrance.

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.lethality_risk: Low, by analogy with the deletion.
routes.specificity: Limb only.
routes.difficulty: high, because the loss-of-function side of the map is not the side that was measured. Building it means a new in-vivo panel.
routes.what_we_would_run: Score the Kvon 2020 panel and report rank correlation against the published in-vivo calls - but label it for what it is: a benchmark on the POLYDACTYLY (gain) direction, used as a proxy for whether the model has any grip on this element at all. Reporting it as a limb-loss benchmark would be a category error.
open_questions: Is a model that ranks gain-of-function ZRS variants well also good at loss-of-function ZRS variants? Nothing in the literature we read answers this, and assuming transfer is exactly the kind of assumption that has failed before.

routes.title: Break the CTCF-mediated contact between the ZRS and the SHH promoter
routes.mechanism: The ZRS acts across ~1 Mb, and that action depends on physical contact. Three CTCF sites inside a 12 kb interval of LMBR1 mediate the ZRS-to-SHH-promoter interaction. Homozygous deletion of that interval in humans causes acheiropodia, congenital limb truncation, and the interval does not itself function as an enhancer - the lesion is architectural, not transcriptional.
routes.intervention: Delete or mutate the CTCF sites that anchor the ZRS-promoter loop, leaving the enhancer sequence intact.
routes.predicted_phenotype: In humans: acheiropodia - congenital truncation of hands and feet. In mouse: NO APPARENT ABNORMALITY. This route is the design space's clearest documented failure of species transfer.

evidence.cite: Ushiki A et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:2282, 'Deletion of CTCF sites in the SHH locus alters enhancer-promoter interactions and leads to acheiropodia'
evidence.finding: Fine-mapped the acheiropodia region to 12 kb; it does not function as an enhancer. Three CTCF sites mediate the ZRS-SHH promoter interaction, substituted by centromeric sites in disease. 'Mouse knockouts of the orthologous 12 kb sequence have no apparent abnormalities, showcasing the challenges in modelling CTCF alterations in animal models due to inherent motif differences between species.'

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable in mouse (no phenotype). In humans acheiropodia is compatible with life.
routes.specificity: Would be limb-restricted if it worked, because the contact being broken is the limb enhancer's.
routes.difficulty: high, and currently unsolved: nobody has engineered a mouse allele that reproduces the human architectural lesion. It would require re-deriving the CTCF motif arrangement for the mouse locus rather than copying the human deletion.
routes.what_we_would_run: Encode this as an explicit REFUSAL in our cross-scale coupling layer: a human-to-mouse transfer of a CTCF-motif-dependent claim is not composable, and the layer should say so with the Ushiki result as the stated reason rather than emitting a score. This is a one-record change and it is the kind of thing the layer exists for.
open_questions: Which mouse CTCF sites would have to be removed to phenocopy acheiropodia? Nobody has published an answer.
Would a sequence model trained on human data flag the mouse orthologous deletion as benign? If it does, that is the correct answer and worth demonstrating.

routes.title: Move a TAD boundary so the limb enhancer cluster drives the wrong gene
routes.mechanism: Limb enhancers are confined to a topologically associating domain by CTCF-associated boundaries. Deletions, inversions and duplications that disrupt those boundaries let a cluster of limb enhancers contact a promoter it should never reach, producing ectopic limb expression of the wrong gene. The rewiring occurs only when the variant disrupts a CTCF-associated boundary - the structural change, not the sequence content, is the lesion.
routes.intervention: CRISPR engineering of deletions, inversions or duplications at a TAD boundary, modelled on the human WNT6/IHH/EPHA4/PAX3 rearrangements, which were reproduced as mouse alleles.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Limb MALFORMATION of a type set by which gene is misexpressed (the published human conditions at this locus are brachydactyly, polydactyly and syndactyly) - not limb loss. This route is in the design space because it is the general architectural mechanism and because it is mouse-validated, not because it has been shown to remove a limb.

evidence.cite: Lupianez DG et al. 2015, Cell 161:1012-1025, 'Disruptions of topological chromatin domains cause pathogenic rewiring of gene-enhancer interactions'
evidence.finding: Distinct human limb malformations are caused by deletions, inversions or duplications altering the TAD-spanning WNT6/IHH/EPHA4/PAX3 locus; CRISPR mice with corresponding rearrangements showed ectopic promoter-noncoding contacts and ectopic limb expression. 'This rewiring occurred only if the variant disrupted a CTCF-associated boundary domain.'

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.lethality_risk: Locus-dependent; the published alleles are viable.
routes.specificity: Depends entirely on which domain is broken. A boundary move is a blunt instrument: it changes everything in the domain, not one enhancer-promoter pair.
routes.difficulty: high. Large structural variants are harder to make and harder to genotype than a 1.3 kb replacement, and the outcome is not predictable from sequence alone.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing yet. A sequence model that scores 1 kb windows has no representation of a megabase-scale boundary, so this route is a good argument for why 'score the enhancer' is not the same as 'predict the phenotype', and it belongs on the page as that argument.
open_questions: Can any current sequence model predict the direction of a boundary-disruption phenotype? We found no evidence that one can, and our search did not cover the chromatin-model literature.

routes.title: Delete the Pitx1 hindlimb enhancer - nature's own cis-regulatory limb removal
routes.mechanism: In threespine stickleback, pelvic (hindlimb-homologue) loss has evolved repeatedly through deletion of a tissue-specific enhancer of Pitx1. Pitx1 null alleles are lethal in laboratory animals; the enhancer deletion is not, and it carries molecular signatures of positive selection. This is the proof of principle that evolution solves 'remove an appendage without killing the animal' by cis-regulation, not by knockout.
routes.intervention: Identify and delete the mouse orthologous hindlimb-specific Pitx1 enhancer. The stickleback element is characterised; the mouse equivalent would have to be mapped, which is work, not a copy.
routes.predicted_phenotype: In stickleback: pelvic reduction/loss, viable, naturally selected. In mouse: UNKNOWN and not to be asserted. The best-supported expectation is a hindlimb-restricted phenotype milder than the Pitx1 null (which gives hindlimb hypoplasia, not absence), but we found no published mouse Pitx1 limb-enhancer deletion.

evidence.cite: Chan YF et al. 2010, Science 327:302-5, 'Adaptive evolution of pelvic reduction in sticklebacks by recurrent deletion of a Pitx1 enhancer'
evidence.finding: Pelvic loss in different natural stickleback populations occurred through regulatory mutations deleting a tissue-specific Pitx1 enhancer. 'Although Pitx1 null mutations are lethal in laboratory animals, Pitx1 regulatory mutations show molecular signatures of positive selection in pelvic-reduced populations.' Deletion is recurrent, possibly from structural features of the locus.

evidence.cite: Lanctot C et al. 1999, Development 126:1805-10, 'Hindlimb patterning and mandible development require the Ptx1 gene'
evidence.finding: Mouse Pitx1 (Ptx1) null: hindlimb development severely impaired but not abolished - ilium and knee cartilage absent, long bones underdeveloped, Tbx4 expression decreased; also loss of proximal mandibular bones. Limb-bud molecular identity is retained.

routes.reversibility: None in the animal.
routes.specificity: Hindlimb only, if the mouse element behaves like the stickleback one. Note the mouse Pitx1 null ALSO loses proximal mandibular bone, so the gene is not hindlimb-exclusive even if the enhancer is.
routes.lethality_risk: Low for an enhancer deletion by the stickleback precedent; high for the null in laboratory animals per Chan et al.
routes.difficulty: high, because the mouse enhancer has to be found first and the Ushiki result (above) is a standing warning that a cis-element's behaviour does not transfer between species.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the single best test case for a sequence model doing something useful rather than reproducing a known answer: use the model to nominate candidate hindlimb-specific Pitx1 enhancers in mouse, then check the nominations against published limb-bud ATAC/ChIP data. That is a retrieval task with an external answer key, not a self-graded one.
open_questions: Is there a single mouse Pitx1 hindlimb enhancer, or distributed redundancy? Enhancer redundancy is the standard reason a cis-deletion gives no phenotype, and we did not search the Pitx1 regulatory-landscape literature.

routes.title: Fgf10 germline null - the canonical tetra-amelia mouse
routes.mechanism: FGF10 is the mesenchymal signal that induces and sustains the apical ectodermal ridge (AER); it acts epistatically upstream of Fgf8, the earliest AER marker. Without it the AER never forms, the ZPA never forms, and the limb bud makes no outgrowth. The same ligand drives branching morphogenesis in lung, so the mouse has no lungs either.
routes.intervention: Germline Fgf10 knockout (two independent lines published, 1998 and 1999).
routes.predicted_phenotype: AMELIA. Fetuses develop to birth with complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs. The clavicle is unaffected (it is a dermal bone of different origin). Perinatal lethal from complete absence of lungs: the trachea forms, main-stem bronchial formation and all subsequent branching do not.

evidence.cite: Min H et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3156-61, 'Fgf-10 is required for both limb and lung development...'
evidence.finding: 'Limb bud initiation was abolished in Fgf-10(-/-) mice. Strikingly, Fgf-10(-/-) fetuses continued to develop until birth, despite the complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs. Fgf-10 is necessary for apical ectodermal ridge (AER) formation and acts epistatically upstream of Fgf-8.' Perinatal lethality with complete absence of lungs.

evidence.cite: Sekine K et al. 1999, Nat Genet 21:138-41, 'Fgf10 is essential for limb and lung formation'
evidence.finding: 'complete truncation of the fore- and hindlimbs. In Fgf10-/- embryos, limb bud formation was initiated but outgrowth of the limb buds did not occur ... the apical ectodermal ridge (AER) and the zone of polarizing activity (ZPA) did not form'; clavicle formation unaffected; died at birth from lack of lung development.

routes.reversibility: None. Germline, constitutive, and the animal cannot be rescued because the lung defect is independent of the limb defect.
routes.lethality_risk: HIGH and certain: perinatal lethal from lung agenesis. No Fgf10-null mouse has ever drawn a breath, so there is no viable limbless adult by this route.
routes.specificity: Poor. FGF10 is the major ligand for FGFR2b across many organs: Fgf10-null mice also lack thyroid, pituitary and salivary glands, with minor defects in teeth, kidney, hair follicles and digestive organs.
routes.difficulty: low to make, impossible to make viable as a constitutive allele. The conditional version is the route worth proposing (see timing-prx1-creer-fgf10).
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing computational adds value here; this is the ground-truth amelia phenotype the whole page is calibrated against. If the judge's mice were tetra-amelic AND died at birth, this is the likely mechanism class.
open_questions: The two founding papers DISAGREE about whether the limb bud initiates: Min et al. say initiation was abolished; Sekine et al. say bud formation initiated but outgrowth did not occur. We preserve that disagreement rather than reconciling it, and it matters because it decides whether the lesion is in induction or in maintenance.

routes.title: Fgfr2-IIIb (FGFR2b) isoform null - the receptor side of the same axis
routes.mechanism: Fgfr2 is alternatively spliced into IIIb and IIIc isoforms with different ligand specificities and mutually exclusive tissue distributions. FGFR2b is the epithelial receptor that reads mesenchymal FGF10. Removing only IIIb leaves IIIc intact and so removes one arm of the mesenchymal-epithelial dialogue rather than the whole receptor.
routes.intervention: Cre-mediated excision of the IIIb exon, retaining IIIc expression.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Severe limb defects with a distinctive time course: 'development of these structures appears to initiate, but then fails with the tissues undergoing extensive apoptosis'. Viable until birth. Also severe lung and anterior pituitary defects, plus salivary gland, inner ear, tooth, skin and minor skull abnormalities.

evidence.cite: De Moerlooze L et al. 2000, Development 127:483-92, 'An important role for the IIIb isoform of fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 (FGFR2) in mesenchymal-epithelial signalling during mouse organogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'Fibroblast growth factor receptor 2(IIIb) null mice are viable until birth, but have severe defects of the limbs, lung and anterior pituitary gland. The development of these structures appears to initiate, but then fails with the tissues undergoing extensive apoptosis.'

evidence.cite: Ohuchi H et al. 2000, Biochem Biophys Res Commun 277:643-9, 'FGF10 acts as a major ligand for FGF receptor 2 IIIb in mouse multi-organ development'
evidence.finding: Fgf10-null phenotypes closely parallel FGFR2b-deficient phenotypes across many organs (absent thyroid, pituitary, salivary glands), supporting FGF10 as the major FGFR2b ligand in organogenesis.

routes.reversibility: None as a germline allele.
routes.lethality_risk: High - viable until birth only, with lung and pituitary agenesis.
routes.specificity: Poor; multi-organ, by construction (the whole point of the receptor is that it serves many epithelia).
routes.difficulty: low to make; same viability dead end as Fgf10.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing new. This route earns its place by being the mechanistic mirror of Fgf10 and by showing that 'initiates then apoptoses' is a THIRD phenotypic class distinct from both amelia and truncation - a distinction the existing dossier does not draw.
open_questions: Is the limb defect in Fgfr2-IIIb nulls the same as the Fgf10 null, or milder because other FGFR2b ligands partially compensate? The abstracts do not settle it and we did not read the bodies.

routes.title: Ectodermal WNT3 / beta-catenin - the human tetra-amelia gene
routes.mechanism: Wnt3 is expressed ubiquitously in limb ectoderm and signals through beta-catenin to establish the AER; beta-catenin is also required continuously to MAINTAIN the ridge once induced. Wnt/beta-catenin sits upstream of BMP signalling in AER establishment and interacts with BMPR1A in dorsoventral patterning. In humans a homozygous nonsense allele of WNT3 causes complete absence of all four limbs.
routes.intervention: Mouse: Wnt3 loss, or conditional removal of beta-catenin from ventral limb ectoderm (before induction to prevent the AER, after induction to make an existing AER disappear). Human: the natural WNT3 Q83X allele.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Human WNT3 Q83X homozygotes: TETRA-AMELIA - complete absence of all four limbs, with craniofacial and urogenital defects. Mouse: AER fails to be established; removing beta-catenin after induction makes an existing AER disappear, giving a later and milder truncation. Note Wnt3-null mice are reported early-lethal, which is why the human allele is the informative one.

evidence.cite: Niemann S et al. 2004, Am J Hum Genet 74:558-63, 'Homozygous WNT3 mutation causes tetra-amelia in a large consanguineous family'
evidence.finding: Homozygous nonsense mutation Q83X in WNT3 in four affected fetuses with autosomal recessive tetra-amelia plus craniofacial and urogenital defects. 'Our findings contrast with the observation of early lethality in mice homozygous for null alleles of Wnt3.' First WNT-gene mutation associated with a Mendelian disorder.

evidence.cite: Barrow JR et al. 2003, Genes Dev 17:394-409, 'Ectodermal Wnt3/beta-catenin signaling is required for the establishment and maintenance of the apical ectodermal ridge'
evidence.finding: Conditional removal of beta-catenin in ventral ectodermal cells is sufficient to elicit the mutant limb phenotype; removing beta-catenin AFTER ridge induction results in the disappearance of the AER. Wnt/beta-catenin lies upstream of BMP in AER establishment.

evidence.cite: Soshnikova N et al. 2003, Genes Dev 17:1963-8, 'Genetic interaction between Wnt/beta-catenin and BMP receptor signaling during formation of the AER and the dorsal-ventral axis in the limb'
evidence.finding: beta-catenin is a key regulator of AER formation and of limb dorsoventral axis; it acts downstream of BMPR1A in AER induction but upstream or parallel in dorsoventral patterning.

routes.reversibility: The beta-catenin conditional is the reversible-in-principle version and the only published demonstration that an ALREADY FORMED AER can be made to disappear - which is the cell-biological basis for every timing route on this page.
routes.lethality_risk: High for germline Wnt3 (early embryonic lethal in mouse). The ectoderm-restricted beta-catenin conditional avoids that.
routes.specificity: beta-catenin is the least specific molecule in this entire design space - it is the canonical WNT effector in essentially every tissue. Restriction comes entirely from the Cre driver, not from the gene.
routes.difficulty: medium. Floxed beta-catenin and limb-ectoderm Cre drivers are standard.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing new computationally. The value of this route on the page is that it names the human condition the judge is most likely to have in mind if their work is human genetics, and that it separates AER ESTABLISHMENT from AER MAINTENANCE as two different targets.
open_questions: The human-versus-mouse viability discordance for WNT3 is flagged by Niemann et al. themselves and is a second instance of the Ushiki lesson: the same gene, two species, different tolerability.

routes.title: RSPO2 / RNF43 / ZNRF3 - the master switch for limb specification
routes.mechanism: RSPO2 potentiates WNT signalling. An allelic series of recessive human RSPO2 mutations causes tetra-amelia syndrome with lung aplasia, with severity correlating with impaired binding to LGR4/5/6 and to the RNF43 and ZNRF3 transmembrane ligases. Unexpectedly, triple knockout of Lgr4/5/6 in mice does NOT reproduce the Rspo2 phenotype; instead RSPO2 acts as a direct antagonistic ligand of RNF43 and ZNRF3, and deleting rnf43 and znrf3 together in Xenopus triggers outgrowth of SUPERNUMERARY limbs.
routes.intervention: Mouse: Rspo2 loss of function, or an allelic series modelled on the human mutations. The reciprocal (deleting Rnf43/Znrf3) is the limb-ADDITION direction and is the cleanest published demonstration that this node is a bidirectional switch.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Human RSPO2 loss of function: tetra-amelia syndrome - 'lung aplasia and a total absence of the four limbs'. The published allelic series means severity is graded, not binary. In mouse, the corresponding Rspo2 limb phenotype is not stated in the abstract we read; we would not assert it.

evidence.cite: Szenker-Ravi E et al. 2018, Nature 557:564-569, 'RSPO2 inhibition of RNF43 and ZNRF3 governs limb development independently of LGR4/5/6'
evidence.finding: 'an allelic series of recessive RSPO2 mutations in humans that cause tetra-amelia syndrome, which is characterized by lung aplasia and a total absence of the four limbs'; severity correlated with binding and WNT-potentiation defects. 'the concurrent deletion of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus embryos was sufficient to trigger the outgrowth of supernumerary limbs. Our results establish that RSPO2 ... serves as a direct antagonistic ligand to RNF43 and ZNRF3, which together constitute a master switch that governs limb specification.'

routes.reversibility: Conceptually the most reversible node in the design space, because it is a ligand-receptor antagonism rather than a transcriptional commitment: the Xenopus result shows the switch can be driven in the gain direction too. Whether that is tractable in mouse is untested.
routes.lethality_risk: High in the full loss-of-function state - lung aplasia accompanies the human amelia, the same coupling as Fgf10. A graded allele from the human series is the way round it, which is what makes the allelic series valuable.
routes.specificity: Whole-organism WNT modulation; not limb-restricted.
routes.difficulty: medium-high. Point alleles from the human series are straightforward to knock in; interpreting them needs the lung phenotype controlled.
routes.what_we_would_run: If a sequence/protein model is going to be tested on 'does this variant abolish limb development', the RSPO2 allelic series is a better-posed coding benchmark than anything in the ZRS literature, because severity is graded, the biochemistry is measured per allele, and the phenotype is recorded per family.
open_questions: What is the mouse Rspo2 limb phenotype, and does it match the human? We did not retrieve it; stating it would be fabrication.
This gene is absent from the existing dossier and is arguably a stronger candidate than WNT3 for 'the gene for limblessness' in human genetics.

routes.title: Tbx5 - forelimb only, and the cleanest single-pair route
routes.mechanism: TBX5 is expressed exclusively in the prospective forelimb mesenchyme before any bud is visible. It directly activates Fgf10 through a conserved binding site, which is how it initiates the FGF/WNT loop. Critically, the limb FIELD is still patterned correctly in its absence: the territory is specified, the bud is simply never started. Tbx5 is also required later for continued outgrowth.
routes.intervention: Germline Tbx5 null, or Cre-conditional deletion in the forelimb field. Human TBX5 haploinsufficiency gives Holt-Oram syndrome (upper-limb and heart defects), which is a much milder phenotype and should not be quoted as limblessness.
routes.predicted_phenotype: FORELIMB BUDS DO NOT FORM. Hindlimbs are normal. Patterning of the lateral plate mesoderm into the limb field is intact; the FGF and Wnt regulatory loops are never established, including initiation of Fgf10 expression. Early forelimb-versus-hindlimb identity is not disturbed.

evidence.cite: Agarwal P et al. 2003, Development 130:623-33, 'Tbx5 is essential for forelimb bud initiation following patterning of the limb field in the mouse embryo'
evidence.finding: 'mouse embryos lacking Tbx5 do not form forelimb buds, although the patterning of the lateral plate mesoderm into the limb field is intact. Tbx5 is not essential for an early establishment of forelimb versus hindlimb identity. In the absence of Tbx5, the FGF and Wnt regulatory loops required for limb bud outgrowth are not established, including initiation of Fgf10 expression. Tbx5 directly activates the Fgf10 gene via a conserved binding site.'

evidence.cite: Rallis C et al. 2003, Development 130:2741-51, 'Tbx5 is required for forelimb bud formation and continued outgrowth'
evidence.finding: Conditional knockout in the developing forelimb shows Tbx5 is required at early limb bud stages for forelimb bud development; dominant-negative/dominant-active misexpression in chick wing shows a further requirement at later stages for continued outgrowth. Human TBX5 haploinsufficiency causes Holt-Oram syndrome.

routes.reversibility: A conditional allele plus an inducible Cre makes this the best-documented STAGE-SELECTABLE single-pair route, because Rallis et al. show there are two separable requirements (initiation and continued outgrowth).
routes.lethality_risk: Medium. TBX5 is a cardiac transcription factor and the germline null has heart defects; a limb-restricted conditional removes that problem. This is the whole argument for conditional over germline.
routes.specificity: Forelimb only - the single most specific route in the gene scale. Hindlimbs untouched.
routes.difficulty: low-medium. Floxed Tbx5 and limb Cre drivers are standard reagents.
routes.what_we_would_run: Our pattern simulators can model an initiation failure (no FGF10 source) versus a maintenance failure (source decays) and ask whether the two give distinguishable bud-size trajectories. That is a model-internal claim about our own simulator, not a claim about mice, and we would label it as such.
open_questions: A forelimb-only animal still has hindlimbs and so can locomote, thermoregulate and reach food - which is why this route, not tetra-amelia, is the one with a plausible welfare case. Whether a mouse without forelimbs can groom adequately is a question for a veterinary assessment, not for us.

routes.title: Tbx4 (with Pitx1) - hindlimb only, and a very narrow time window
routes.mechanism: Tbx4 is the hindlimb counterpart of Tbx5 and is required for hindlimb bud outgrowth; Pitx1 sits with it in the posterior lateral plate and determines hindlimb morphological identity. The conditional analysis is the interesting part: ablating Tbx4 before hindlimb-field expression blocks outgrowth, ablating it shortly after onset leaves outgrowth and Fgf10 expression unaffected but reduces limb core tissue, and ablating it later produces no defect at all.
routes.intervention: Germline Tbx4 null; or the conditional allele ablated at chosen stages; or Pitx1 null. Pitx1 misexpression in the forelimb transforms forelimb muscle, tendon and bone towards hindlimb morphology, so the gene is a morphology switch in both directions.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Tbx4 null: the hindlimb field IS induced and initial bud patterning appears normal, but buds fail to develop and do not maintain Fgf10; embryos die by E10.5 from failed chorioallantoic fusion, with stunted apoptotic allantoises and no vascular remodelling. Pitx1 null: hindlimb development severely impaired but NOT abolished - ilium and knee cartilage absent, long bones underdeveloped, Tbx4 reduced. Tbx4 loss does not alter hindlimb IDENTITY by morphology or molecular markers.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2003, Development 130:2681-93, 'Loss of Tbx4 blocks hindlimb development and affects vascularization and fusion of the allantois'
evidence.finding: Homozygous nulls 'fail to undergo chorioallantoic fusion and die by 10.5 days post coitus'. 'Induction of a hindlimb field occurs normally in Tbx4 mutants and initial patterning of the hindlimb bud appears normal. However, hindlimb buds from Tbx4 mutants fail to develop either in vivo or in vitro and do not maintain Fgf10 expression in the mesenchyme.'

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2007, Development 134:93-103, 'Tbx4 is not required for hindlimb identity or post-bud hindlimb outgrowth'
evidence.finding: Ablation before hindlimb-field expression confirms a requirement for bud outgrowth; ablation shortly after onset 'alters neither limb outgrowth nor expression of Fgf10' but gives reduced limb core tissue and proximal hypoplasia; later loss 'produces no limb defects, revealing a brief developmental requirement for Tbx4 function'. Loss of Tbx4 has no effect on hindlimb identity.

evidence.cite: Lanctot C et al. 1999, Development 126:1805-10
evidence.finding: Pitx1 null: hindlimb severely impaired not abolished; ilium and knee cartilage absent; also loss of proximal mandible-derived bones.

evidence.cite: DeLaurier A, Schweitzer R & Logan M 2006, Dev Biol 299:22-34, 'Pitx1 determines the morphology of muscle, tendon, and bones of the hindlimb'
evidence.finding: Misexpression of Pitx1 in the forelimb transforms and translocates specific muscles, tendons and bones toward hindlimb-like morphology and upregulates Hoxc10 and Tbx4; misexpression of Tbx4 does not. 'Pitx1, but not Tbx4, determines the morphological identity of hindlimb tissues.'

routes.reversibility: The published conditional series is the point: there is a brief window in which Tbx4 matters and outside it the gene is dispensable. That is a real, measured timing knob, not a proposal.
routes.lethality_risk: The germline Tbx4 null is lethal at E10.5 for an allantoic reason entirely unrelated to limbs - a textbook case of a non-limb phenotype masquerading as a limb result. The conditional allele is what makes the route usable at all.
routes.specificity: Hindlimb only, if conditional. The germline allele also hits the allantois; Pitx1 also hits the mandible.
routes.difficulty: medium. Conditional allele and stage-specific Cre both published.
routes.what_we_would_run: Encode the Tbx4 timing result as a test case for our coupling layer: the SAME genetic lesion produces three different phenotypes depending only on when it is applied. Any claim of the form 'gene X -> phenotype Y' that carries no time index should be refused by the layer, and this is the cleanest published example to anchor that rule on.
open_questions: Is there an equivalently narrow window for Tbx5 in the forelimb? Rallis et al. report two requirements but we did not find a stage-resolved series as fine as Naiche's.

routes.title: Meis1 + Meis2 in the lateral plate mesoderm - limb agenesis upstream of everything
routes.mechanism: MEIS factors act before limb induction. They co-bind genomic sites extensively with TBX factors and co-regulate Fgf10 enhancers, so removing both from the lateral plate mesoderm removes the input that lets Tbx5/Tbx4 start a bud at all. A partial allele also disrupts the antero-posterior prepattern that Shh activation depends on, which is a second, separable requirement.
routes.intervention: Conditional inactivation of Meis1 and Meis2 in the lateral plate mesoderm; or a three-deleted-allele hypomorph for the graded version.
routes.predicted_phenotype: LIMB AGENESIS (both pairs) on full inactivation in the LPM. Three-deleted-allele limbs show proximal-specific skeletal hypoplasia and agenesis of POSTERIOR skeletal elements, from failure to establish the AP prepattern needed for Shh activation. So the same gene pair gives agenesis or a graded posterior loss depending on dose.

evidence.cite: Delgado I et al. 2021, Nat Commun 12:3086, 'Control of mouse limb initiation and antero-posterior patterning by Meis transcription factors'
evidence.finding: 'Meis1/2 inactivation in the lateral plate mesoderm of mouse embryos leads to limb agenesis. Meis and Tbx factors converge in this function, extensively co-binding with Tbx to genomic sites and co-regulating enhancers of Fgf10 ... Limbs with three deleted Meis alleles show proximal-specific skeletal hypoplasia and agenesis of posterior skeletal elements.'

evidence.cite: Berenguer M & Duester G 2021, Biomolecules 11:80, 'Role of Retinoic Acid Signaling, FGF Signaling and Meis Genes in Control of Limb Development' (review)
evidence.finding: Review arguing that activation of FGF10 signalling is required for limb-bud emergence, with Tbx5/RA upstream in the forelimb field and Tbx4/Pitx1 upstream in the hindlimb field; and that limb Meis expression is activated proximally by a factor other than RA and repressed distally by FGF8.

routes.reversibility: Conditional by construction - the published allele is already a Cre-conditional in the LPM, so an inducible version is a reagent swap rather than a new design.
routes.lethality_risk: Medium-high; Meis factors are broad organogenesis regulators and the LPM gives rise to much more than limbs. We did not retrieve viability data and will not assert it.
routes.specificity: LPM-restricted rather than limb-restricted - a larger territory than Prx1-Cre.
routes.difficulty: medium-high: a two-gene conditional cross with four floxed alleles plus a driver.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the best published example of DOSE producing a qualitatively different phenotype (agenesis versus posterior-element loss), which is the shape of claim our Lean threshold-interval family is written for. Stating that as a law about a model - monotone activity to ordered element count - and then mutating the law to check Lean rejects the mutants is a real, bounded job, and it proves consistency of our reasoning, not anything about mice.
open_questions: Does the Meis dose series have a measured activity readout, or only allele count? A threshold law needs a continuous variable and allele count is a proxy.

routes.title: Fgf4 + Fgf8 in the AER - remove the ridge's output and limb development fails
routes.mechanism: The AER's job is to make FGFs. Four Fgf genes have AER-specific expression; only Fgf8 is expressed throughout the ridge and earliest. Inactivating Fgf8 alone reduces bud size, delays Shh and gives hypoplasia or aplasia of specific skeletal elements. Inactivating Fgf4 and Fgf8 together in AER cells or their precursors removes the output entirely: the bud has too few progenitors and cells far from the ridge die.
routes.intervention: Conditional inactivation of Fgf8 in limb ectoderm, or Fgf4 and Fgf8 together in AER cells or their precursors, at chosen stages.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Fgf8 alone: substantial reduction in limb-bud size, delayed Shh, misregulated Fgf4, hypoplasia or aplasia of SPECIFIC skeletal elements - a partial, element-selective loss. Both together: 'In the complete absence of both FGF4 and FGF8 activities, limb development fails.' Severity scales with how early the inactivation happens, because the lesion is progenitor number and survival.

evidence.cite: Sun X, Mariani FV & Martin GR 2002, Nature 418:501-8, 'Functions of FGF signalling from the apical ectodermal ridge in limb development'
evidence.finding: 'FGF4 and FGF8 regulate cell number in the nascent limb bud and are required for survival of cells located far from the AER ... In the complete absence of both FGF4 and FGF8 activities, limb development fails.' Inactivation was performed at different stages.

evidence.cite: Lewandoski M, Sun X & Martin GR 2000, Nat Genet 26:460-3, 'Fgf8 signalling from the AER is essential for normal limb development'
evidence.finding: Inactivating Fgf8 in early limb ectoderm 'causes a substantial reduction in limb-bud size, a delay in Shh expression, misregulation of Fgf4 expression, and hypoplasia or aplasia of specific skeletal elements'. Loss of Fgf4, Fgf9 or Fgf17 alone has no effect on limb formation.

evidence.cite: Lu P, Minowada G & Martin GR 2006, Development 133:33-42, 'Increasing Fgf4 expression in the mouse limb bud causes polysyndactyly and rescues the skeletal defects that result from loss of Fgf8 function'
evidence.finding: Expressing Fgf4 in place of Fgf8 rescues all skeletal defects caused by Fgf8 inactivation, so FGF4 can functionally replace FGF8. Raising FGF signalling in a wild-type bud causes postaxial polydactyly and cutaneous syndactyly: 'the importance of controlling the level of FGF gene expression for normal limb development'.

routes.reversibility: Not reversible once progenitors are dead - the lesion is cell number, and lost cells do not come back. This is the clearest case on the page of an irreversible cellular commitment, as opposed to a transcriptional state.
routes.lethality_risk: Low-medium when restricted to limb ectoderm; Fgf8 has major non-limb roles so the driver carries the risk, not the gene.
routes.specificity: Both limbs; element-selective at intermediate doses, which makes it a partial-loss route rather than an all-or-nothing one.
routes.difficulty: medium-high: two floxed genes plus an AER-specific driver, and the stage of inactivation has to be controlled because it sets severity.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the one route whose mechanism is explicitly QUANTITATIVE - cell number and survival - and so the one our reaction-diffusion and growth simulators can actually represent. We can simulate bud size as a function of FGF source strength and ask at what point the pattern-forming domain falls below the size that supports digit condensations. That is a simulated result and would be labelled as such; we have no calibration that would let us attach a skeletal count to it.
open_questions: Lu et al. show FGF4 can replace FGF8 entirely, so AER-FGF identity does not matter but AER-FGF LEVEL does. Any model that scores per-gene rather than per-total-dose will get this wrong.

routes.title: Grem1 - remove the BMP antagonist and the mesenchyme kills itself
routes.mechanism: Mesenchymal GREMLIN1 antagonises BMP, and that antagonism is what permits a functional AER to form and the SHH/FGF feedback loop to propagate. Without it the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback never gets going and the core limb-bud mesenchyme is eliminated by apoptosis - the same fate as the metanephric mesenchyme in the same mutant.
routes.intervention: Grem1 germline null, or conditional deletion in limb mesenchyme.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Failure to establish a functional AER and the SHH/FGF loop; core mesenchyme eliminated by apoptosis. Neonatal lethal from absence of kidneys, with lung septation defects.

evidence.cite: Michos O et al. 2004, Development 131:3401-10, 'Gremlin-mediated BMP antagonism induces the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signaling controlling metanephric kidney and limb organogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'A Grem1 null mutation in the mouse ... causes neonatal lethality because of the lack of kidneys and lung septation defects. In early limb buds, mesenchymal Grem1 is required to establish a functional apical ectodermal ridge and the epithelial-mesenchymal feedback signaling that propagates the sonic hedgehog morphogen'; the metanephric mesenchyme 'is eliminated by apoptosis, in the same way as the core mesenchymal cells of the limb bud'.

routes.reversibility: None as germline. Apoptotic loss of the mesenchymal core is not recoverable.
routes.lethality_risk: HIGH and certain: neonatal lethal from renal agenesis. Another case where the limb phenotype is never seen in a living adult.
routes.specificity: Poor; the same BMP-antagonism requirement operates in kidney and lung.
routes.difficulty: low to make, not viable.
routes.what_we_would_run: Grem1 is the inhibitor arm of the self-terminating loop (see tissue-shh-grem1-fgf-loop), so it is the parameter our activator-inhibitor simulators would move first. We can run it; we cannot calibrate it, and we would say so.
open_questions: A limb-mesenchyme-restricted conditional should separate the limb from the kidney phenotype; our search did not retrieve one and we will not assume it exists.

routes.title: Shh null (and why Gli3 shows this is the wrong route)
routes.mechanism: Deleting Shh removes distal limb structures, but it also removes the organiser of the notochord, floor plate, neural tube and axial skeleton, giving cyclopia and loss of the spinal column and most ribs. More importantly, the limb part of the phenotype is PERMISSIVE rather than instructive: disrupting one or both Gli3 alleles in a Shh-null background progressively restores distal limb development and digit formation. SHH's limb role is to counteract GLI3 repression, not to build a limb.
routes.intervention: Shh germline null; Shh;Gli3 double mutants; Gli3 null (extra toes, Xt) alone.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Shh null: absence of distal limb structures, PLUS cyclopia, absence of ventral neural tube cell types, and absence of the spinal column and most ribs. Gli3 null alone: pronounced POLYDACTYLY with loss of digit identity and ectopic anterior Shh - the opposite direction. Shh-/-;Gli3-/-: distal limb development and digits progressively restored.

evidence.cite: Chiang C et al. 1996, Nature 383:407-13, 'Cyclopia and defective axial patterning in mice lacking Sonic hedgehog gene function'
evidence.finding: Shh null: 'absence of distal limb structures, cyclopia, absence of ventral cell types within the neural tube, and absence of the spinal column and most of the ribs', with early defects in notochord and floorplate.

evidence.cite: te Welscher P et al. 2002, Science 298:827-30, 'Progression of vertebrate limb development through SHH-mediated counteraction of GLI3'
evidence.finding: 'the polydactyly of Gli3-deficient mice arises independently of SHH signaling. Disruption of one or both Gli3 alleles in mouse embryos lacking Shh progressively restores limb distal development and digit formation ... SHH signaling counteracts GLI3-mediated repression of key regulator genes, cell survival, and distal progression.'

evidence.cite: Buscher D et al. 1997, Mech Dev 62:175-82, 'Evidence for genetic control of Sonic hedgehog by Gli3 in mouse limb development'
evidence.finding: Shh and Gli3 expression domains are mutually exclusive in the limb bud; in Gli3-null extra toes (Xt) mice Shh is ectopically expressed anteriorly, with Ptc, Fgf, Bmp and Hoxd misexpressed accordingly.

evidence.cite: Hill P, Gotz K & Ruther U 2009, Dev Biol 328:506-16, 'A SHH-independent regulation of Gli3 is a significant determinant of anteroposterior patterning of the limb bud'
evidence.finding: Quantitative demand for GLI3 varies across phases of distal limb formation; unprocessed full-length GLI3 is dispensable for AP patterning and digit identities are most likely defined by GLI3 repressor activity alone; Gli3 is also regulated independently of SHH.

routes.reversibility: None as germline; Shh conditional alleles are the reversible version and are covered under cell-zpa-shh-timing.
routes.lethality_risk: Very high and for reasons unrelated to limbs - cyclopia and axial skeleton loss. Nobody should propose Shh-null as a route to a limbless mouse, and the page should say so explicitly because it is the gene everyone names first.
routes.specificity: Terrible. This is the least limb-specific route in the design space, which is exactly why the ZRS exists as an alternative: the enhancer separates the limb function from all the others.
routes.difficulty: low to make, useless as an animal.
routes.what_we_would_run: Use the Shh/ZRS contrast as the page's central argument: the SAME gene, approached through its coding sequence or through one of its enhancers, gives a dead cyclopic embryo or a viable limb-reduced mouse. That contrast is the strongest single thing we can show a judge about why cis-regulation is the interesting layer.
open_questions: The te Welscher result means ZRS-null truncation is a failure to RELIEVE GLI3 repression rather than a failure to deliver a positive signal. Any model of 'enhancer activity to skeletal element count' that treats SHH as an instructive morphogen has the sign of the mechanism wrong, even if it fits the data.

routes.title: p63 - limbs absent or truncated because the AER never differentiates
routes.mechanism: p63 is expressed in the ectodermal surfaces of the limb buds and is required for the AER to differentiate and to be maintained as a stratified epithelium. The lesion is not induction of the limb field and not mesenchymal signalling: it is the failure of a progenitor epithelium to sustain itself. Mice lacking p63 are BORN ALIVE, which makes this the only amelia-class route on this page that is not immediately lethal for a non-limb reason.
routes.intervention: p63 germline knockout (two independent lines, both 1999). A conditional version restricted to limb ectoderm would be the design worth proposing.
routes.predicted_phenotype: 'Their limbs are absent or truncated, defects that are caused by a failure of the apical ectodermal ridge to differentiate' (Mills et al.); limb truncations 'due to a failure to maintain the apical ectodermal ridge' (Yang et al.). Severe accompanying ectodermal phenotype: no skin stratification, absence of all squamous epithelia and their derivatives including hair follicles, teeth, mammary, lacrimal and salivary glands; craniofacial defects.

evidence.cite: Mills AA et al. 1999, Nature 398:708-13, 'p63 is a p53 homologue required for limb and epidermal morphogenesis'
evidence.finding: 'Mice lacking p63 are born alive but have striking developmental defects. Their limbs are absent or truncated, defects that are caused by a failure of the apical ectodermal ridge to differentiate.' Skin lacks stratification; hair follicles, teeth and mammary glands absent.

evidence.cite: Yang A et al. 1999, Nature 398:714-8, 'p63 is essential for regenerative proliferation in limb, craniofacial and epithelial development'
evidence.finding: 'The limb truncations are due to a failure to maintain the apical ectodermal ridge, a stratified epithelium, essential for limb development'; absence of all squamous epithelia and derivatives; p63 maintains the progenitor-cell populations sustaining epithelial morphogenesis.

routes.reversibility: None as germline.
routes.lethality_risk: High in practice. Born alive, but with no stratified skin and no epidermal appendages a pup cannot maintain barrier function; this is a severe phenotype in the welfare sense even though the embryo reaches term. The two papers report birth, not survival.
routes.specificity: Poor as a germline allele - it is an ectodermal phenotype, of which the limb is one part. A limb-ectoderm conditional would in principle fix this and we found no such study.
routes.difficulty: low as germline; medium for the conditional that would actually be worth making.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing computational. p63 earns its place because it is a THIRD mechanism class the existing dossier omits: not induction failure (Fgf10, Wnt3), not signalling-centre output failure (ZRS, Fgf4/8), but failure of the signalling centre's epithelium to differentiate at all.
open_questions: Why is the phenotype 'absent OR truncated' rather than uniform? Variable expressivity in an amelia-class allele is itself informative and we did not read the bodies to find out.

routes.title: Hand2 - the posterior prepattern, and the gene cetaceans lost
routes.mechanism: HAND2 is a bHLH regulator that establishes anterior and posterior polarity of the nascent limb-bud mesenchyme and sits upstream of SHH. It controls expression of proximal limb genes and sets the Gli3 and Tbx3 expression boundaries that define where the ZPA can form. It functions in dimers with other bHLH factors (TWIST1) in balance with ETS factors, and that balance sets the anterior-posterior pattern.
routes.intervention: Conditional Hand2 deletion in limb mesenchyme; or perturbation of the HAND2/TWIST1/ETV dimerisation balance.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Loss of the posterior prepattern needed for Shh, hence a posteriorly-biased reduction rather than whole-limb loss. We did not retrieve a Hand2 conditional limb skeletal phenotype and will not state one. In the opposite direction, Etv4/Etv5 loss gives preaxial polydactyly which is suppressed by a Hand2 mutation - genetic antagonism, so the node is bidirectional.

evidence.cite: Osterwalder M et al. 2014, Dev Cell 31:345-357, 'HAND2 targets define a network of transcriptional regulators that compartmentalize the early limb bud mesenchyme'
evidence.finding: 'HAND2 controls the expression of genes functioning in the proximal limb bud and orchestrates the establishment of anterior and posterior polarity of the nascent limb bud mesenchyme by impacting Gli3 and Tbx3 expression. TBX3 is required downstream of HAND2 to refine the posterior Gli3 expression boundary.'

evidence.cite: Zhang Z et al. 2010, Development 137:3417-26, 'Preaxial polydactyly: interactions among ETV, TWIST1 and HAND2 control anterior-posterior patterning of the limb'
evidence.finding: Twist1 is required to inhibit anterior Shh; genetic synergism with Etv4/Etv5 via direct TWIST1-ETV association; 'the PPD phenotype observed in Etv mutants is suppressed by a mutation in Hand2, indicative of genetic antagonism'.

evidence.cite: Thewissen JGM et al. 2006, PNAS 103:8414-8, 'Developmental basis for hind-limb loss in dolphins and origin of the cetacean bodyplan'
evidence.finding: In the dolphin hindlimb bud 'Sonic hedgehog (Shh) ... is absent' and 'failure to establish a ZPA is associated with the absence of Hand2, an upstream regulator of Shh'.

routes.reversibility: Conditional alleles exist in the published work; no inducible time-course was retrieved.
routes.lethality_risk: High for germline - HAND2 is required in heart and branchial arches. Limb-restricted conditional is mandatory.
routes.specificity: Limb mesenchyme if conditional; posterior-biased within the limb.
routes.difficulty: medium.
routes.what_we_would_run: Hand2 is the node that links the mouse genetics to the cetacean natural experiment, and the page should draw that line explicitly: whales lost hindlimbs with Hand2 absent from the bud and Shh never established, which is upstream of the ZRS lesion snakes have. Two independent natural limb losses, two different layers of the same network.
open_questions: Is the dolphin Hand2 absence a cause or a consequence? Thewissen et al. report association, and we are reading an abstract. We would not state causation.

routes.title: Cut the AER off at a chosen hour - the original timing experiment
routes.mechanism: The AER is a physical strip of thickened ectoderm at the distal tip of the bud. Excising it stops distal outgrowth from that moment, and what is already specified proximally still forms. The level of the resulting truncation is therefore a function of WHEN the ridge is removed, which makes this the oldest and most direct demonstration that limb loss is a timing problem rather than only a genetic one.
routes.intervention: Microsurgical excision of the AER from a chick limb bud at a staged time point. In mouse this is not practical in utero; the equivalents are the genetic routes (gene-aer-fgf4-fgf8) or explant culture (invitro-limb-bud-explant).
routes.predicted_phenotype: Progressive distal truncation whose level tracks the stage of excision: earlier removal leaves less limb. The classical series is quantitative.

evidence.cite: Summerbell D 1974, J Embryol Exp Morphol 32:651-60, 'A quantitative analysis of the effect of excision of the AER from the chick limb-bud'
evidence.finding: PubMed record retrieved and the title and MeSH terms (Ectoderm, Extremities, Gestational Age, Humerus, Radius, Ulna, Morphogenesis, Wings) confirm a staged quantitative excision series in chick. NO ABSTRACT IS AVAILABLE in the PubMed record, so we have not read any result statement from this paper and we report only what the record itself shows.

evidence.cite: Lewandoski M, Sun X & Martin GR 2000, Nat Genet 26:460-3
evidence.finding: States the classical premise independently: 'Removal of the AER in chick results in limbs lacking distal skeletal elements' and FGF proteins can substitute for the AER.

routes.reversibility: Not reversible once cut, but FGF protein beads substitute for the removed ridge, which is the sufficiency half of the experiment and makes the manipulation effectively two-way in chick.
routes.lethality_risk: Low in chick; the manipulation is local.
routes.specificity: One limb, one bud, at one time - the most spatially and temporally precise intervention available anywhere in this design space.
routes.difficulty: low in chick (a classical embryology technique), impractical in mouse in utero.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the physical ground truth for the timing axis. Our growth simulators can reproduce 'stop distal outgrowth at time t and see what is already specified', and the chick excision series is the only dataset that could calibrate such a model - except that we cannot read Summerbell's numbers from the PubMed record, so the calibration is not available to us today.
open_questions: We could not access the numerical series. Any claim we make about the quantitative relationship between excision stage and truncation level would be unsupported by what we actually read.

routes.title: Kill the AER genetically with a cell-autonomous toxin
routes.mechanism: Instead of cutting the ridge off, express diphtheria toxin A under a promoter active in AER precursors, so the signalling centre is deleted cell-autonomously and without surgery. This is the standard technique for ablating an organiser in the mouse; it has been used to remove the roof plate from the neural tube and to ablate lens precursors before placode formation, both of which produced the expected loss of the structures that depended on the organiser.
routes.intervention: An AER-restricted promoter (for example an Msx2 or limb-ectoderm element) driving attenuated DTA, or a Cre driver crossed to a ROSA26-LoxP-DTA reporter.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED, NOT OBSERVED. By analogy with AER excision the expectation is distal truncation set by the onset of toxin expression, with the proximal skeleton retained. We found NO published AER DTA ablation in our searches and we would not state a phenotype for it.

evidence.cite: Lee KJ, Dietrich P & Jessell TM 2000, Nature 403:734-40, 'Genetic ablation reveals that the roof plate is essential for dorsal interneuron specification'
evidence.finding: A genetic strategy selectively ablated the roof plate in mouse embryos; embryos without a roof plate lack all the interneuron subtypes normally generated in the dorsal third of the neural tube, from loss of non-autonomous signals. Establishes the method for organiser ablation in mouse.

evidence.cite: Zhang Y et al. 2008, Dev Biol 323:53-63, 'Dominant inhibition of lens placode formation in mice'
evidence.finding: Transgenic mice expressing attenuated diphtheria toxin (Tox176) from a modified Pax6 promoter ablated lens precursor cells BEFORE placode formation, allowing the role of the structure to be tested at its earliest stage. Demonstrates that pre-placodal ablation with an attenuated toxin is achievable.

routes.reversibility: None - toxin-killed cells do not return. The control is over WHEN, not whether.
routes.lethality_risk: Depends entirely on promoter leakiness; an attenuated toxin is used precisely to keep ablation local.
routes.specificity: As specific as the promoter. An AER-only driver would be the most limb-specific cellular intervention possible.
routes.difficulty: medium-high, and the honest difficulty is finding a driver that is on in AER precursors and nowhere that matters.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. This route is on the page as a clearly-labelled PROPOSAL, to show the shape of the design space rather than to claim a result. Presenting it as established would be the exact failure mode the page exists to avoid.
open_questions: Does an AER-specific driver with the right onset exist? Our search covered 'diphtheria toxin ablation apical ectodermal ridge genetic mouse' on PubMed and returned four records, none of them an AER ablation. That is the scope of our negative, not a statement about the literature.

routes.title: Remove the ZPA's signal at a chosen stage - digits disappear in a defined order
routes.mechanism: SHH from the ZPA does two separable jobs: a very transient early patterning job that assigns digit identity, and an extended growth-promoting job during which the digit precursor mesenchyme expands and is recruited into condensing digit primordia. Deleting Shh progressively earlier with an inducible Cre removes progressively more digits, and the order in which they are lost mirrors an alternating anterior-posterior sequence of normal digit formation.
routes.intervention: Tamoxifen-inducible Cre (ShhCreER) with a conditional Shh allele, dosed at a chosen embryonic day.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Progressive loss of digits, with the number lost set by how early Shh is removed. Not limb loss: the stylopod and zeugopod are not the target. This route tunes AUTOPOD CONTENT, precisely and reproducibly.

evidence.cite: Zhu J et al. 2008, Dev Cell 14:624-32, 'Uncoupling Sonic hedgehog control of pattern and expansion of the developing limb bud'
evidence.finding: 'Deleting the mouse Shh gene at different times using a conditional Cre line, we find that Shh functions to control limb development in two phases: a very transient, early patterning phase regulating digit identity, and an extended growth-promoting phase ... The progressive loss of digits upon successively earlier Shh removal mirrors this alternating sequence.'

evidence.cite: Scherz PJ et al. 2004, Science 305:396-9, 'The limb bud Shh-Fgf feedback loop is terminated by expansion of former ZPA cells'
evidence.finding: Shh-expressing cells and their descendants cannot express Gremlin; their proliferation forms a physical barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks the Shh-Fgf4 loop and thereby affects limb size.

routes.reversibility: Reversible in the sense that matters for experimental design: the lesion is applied at a time of the experimenter's choosing, not at fertilisation. It is not reversible after the fact.
routes.lethality_risk: Low when induction is late enough to miss the early Shh requirements in notochord and neural tube - which is exactly the advantage of the inducible allele over the germline null (compare gene-shh-gli3, which is catastrophic).
routes.specificity: Autopod, both limbs, graded.
routes.difficulty: low-medium; the alleles are published and tamoxifen dosing is routine.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the best-posed quantitative dataset in the whole design space for our Lean threshold work: an ordered stimulus (induction time) mapping to an ordered, countable outcome (digit number). Stating 'given a monotone map from signal duration to element count, an ordered duration series implies an ordered count series', then mutating the monotonicity and the threshold and showing Lean rejects both mutants, is a bounded job. It proves our reasoning is consistent; it proves nothing about mice, and the page must say that in the same sentence.
open_questions: Scherz et al. make loop termination a consequence of CELL LINEAGE geometry rather than of a transcriptional timer. A model with no spatial representation of former-ZPA descendants cannot express that mechanism at all.

routes.title: Tune the limb by changing how fast the morphogen falls apart
routes.mechanism: FGF10 is an intrinsically unstable protein that unfolds and is rapidly inactivated at 37 C, and the thermodynamic stability of the 22 mammalian FGFs varies widely. Engineered FGF10 variants with a melting temperature more than 19 C above wild type bind receptors, activate signalling and induce gene expression identically in cell assays, yet behave completely differently in tissue - which implies that protein half-life, not receptor affinity, is part of how the limb reads this signal.
routes.intervention: Knock in a stabilised (or, for limb reduction, a destabilised) Fgf10 allele. Stabilised FGF10 variants implanted into chicken limb buds markedly altered limb morphogenesis and inhibited growth of mouse embryonic tibias.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Stabilised direction (measured): suppressed lung branching with increased alveolarisation and epithelial expansion; inhibited embryonic tibia growth; markedly altered limb morphogenesis in chick bud implants. Destabilised direction (PROPOSED, not measured): a graded hypomorphic FGF10 signal, predicted to give partial limb reduction rather than the all-or-nothing amelia of the null.

evidence.cite: Czyrek AA et al. 2025, Cell Mol Life Sci 82:167, 'Increased thermal stability of FGF10 leads to ectopic signaling during development'
evidence.finding: 'FGF10, an important limb and lung morphogen, exists as an intrinsically unstable protein that is prone to unfolding and is rapidly inactivated at 37 C'; STAB variants with +19 C melting temperature were indistinguishable in receptor binding and signalling in cells but 'inhibited the growth of mouse embryonic tibias and markedly altered limb morphogenesis when implanted into chicken limb buds, collectively demonstrating that thermal instability should be considered an important regulator of FGF function that prevents ectopic signaling'.

routes.reversibility: A knock-in allele is not reversible; but recombinant protein delivery is, and the published work is a bead/implant experiment, which is the acute, dose-controlled version.
routes.lethality_risk: Unknown for a destabilised germline allele. If it behaves as a graded Fgf10 hypomorph the lung phenotype scales with it, so the lethality that sinks the Fgf10 null is likely to scale too.
routes.specificity: Poor at the gene level (FGF10 serves many organs) but unusual at the BIOPHYSICAL level: nothing else on this page proposes to tune a phenotype by changing a protein's folding stability rather than its sequence-level function.
routes.difficulty: high, and genuinely novel - we found no published destabilised-FGF10 animal.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the one route where a protein-structure model, rather than a genome model, is the right tool: predict melting temperature for designed FGF10 variants and check against the measured STAB series, which gives a held-out numerical benchmark with real values. We have not run it and have no structure pipeline today.
open_questions: Does a destabilised FGF10 produce a graded limb phenotype, or does the limb buffer ligand half-life entirely? Unknown; the published direction is the stabilising one.

routes.title: Trigger the self-terminating loop early
routes.mechanism: Limb outgrowth is driven by a positive feedback loop between Shh, Gremlin1 and AER-FGFs. The loop is not stopped by an external clock: rising FGF activity itself represses Grem1, so the circuit is self-promoting AND self-terminating. Independently, the descendants of former Shh-expressing cells cannot express Gremlin and physically interpose between the Shh source and the Gremlin domain, breaking the loop geometrically. Either mechanism, triggered early, should stop outgrowth early.
routes.intervention: Raise FGF activity in the early bud to engage the Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop before the limb has grown (a conditional Fgf4 gain-of-function allele exists and is known to raise FGF signalling in the bud); or force premature expansion of the former-ZPA lineage.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED for the deliberate-early-termination direction. The components are measured: compound mutants defective in the positive loop show that FGF signalling represses Grem1 in a manner dependent on high FGF activity, in both mouse and chick. Note that the one published high-FGF4 gain-of-function gave postaxial POLYDACTYLY and syndactyly, not truncation - so 'more FGF' is not simply 'earlier stop', and we would not assert the predicted direction.

evidence.cite: Verheyden JM & Sun X 2008, Nature 454:638-41, 'An Fgf/Gremlin inhibitory feedback loop triggers termination of limb bud outgrowth'
evidence.finding: 'genetic evidence that FGF signalling can repress Grem1 expression, revealing a novel Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop ... dependent on high FGF activity ... the positive Fgf/Shh loop drives outgrowth and an increase in FGF signalling, which triggers the Fgf/Grem1 inhibitory loop ... a self-promoting and self-terminating circuit'.

evidence.cite: Scherz PJ et al. 2004, Science 305:396-9
evidence.finding: Proliferation of former-ZPA descendants 'forms a barrier separating the Shh signal from Gremlin-expressing cells, which breaks down the Shh-Fgf4 loop and thereby affects limb size'.

evidence.cite: Lu P, Minowada G & Martin GR 2006, Development 133:33-42
evidence.finding: A conditional Fgf4 gain-of-function allele activated in a wild-type limb bud 'causes formation of a supernumerary posterior digit (postaxial polydactyly), as well as cutaneous syndactyly between all the digits'.

routes.reversibility: In principle fully reversible, because the target is a dynamic circuit state rather than a genomic lesion - but no published experiment turns the loop off and back on.
routes.lethality_risk: Low if limb-restricted.
routes.specificity: Both limbs; the loop is limb-bud-specific in its Shh/Grem1 arm.
routes.difficulty: high. The circuit is the thing everyone understands least well in quantitative terms, which is why 'trigger it early' is a sentence and not a protocol.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the one route our existing reaction-diffusion and pattern simulators represent natively: an activator-inhibitor system with delayed negative feedback. We can run it and show how termination time moves with the inhibitory-loop gain. We CANNOT calibrate it - we have no registered calibration anywhere in our system - so the output is a simulated trajectory labelled 'simulated, not observed', and the bridge from it to a skeletal element count is exactly the kind our coupling layer refuses.
open_questions: Mouse and chick terminate the loop in a different SEQUENCE, which is what led Verheyden & Sun to the inhibitory loop in the first place. A single model fitted to one species is not transferable to the other without saying so.

routes.title: Detune the digit-patterning Turing network
routes.mechanism: Digits emerge from undifferentiated mesenchyme through a self-organising periodic mechanism. Combined experiment and modelling implicate a Turing network implemented by BMP, SOX9 and WNT, modulated by morphogen gradients; a two-dimensional simulation of this network reproduces wild-type and perturbed Sox9 expression patterns. Changing the network's parameters changes the periodic pattern, and in principle a sufficiently detuned network produces no periodic skeletal pattern at all.
routes.intervention: Pharmacological or genetic modulation of BMP and WNT in the autopod field, guided by the published model.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Changes in DIGIT PATTERN - number, spacing, thickness. NOT limb loss. This route is in the design space because it is the mechanism that decides what the autopod looks like, and because it is the only route here with a published, runnable, quantitative model attached.
