Claiming it produces a limbless mouse would be unsupported.

evidence.cite: Raspopovic J, Marcon L, Russo L & Sharpe J 2014, Science 345:566-70, 'Digit patterning is controlled by a Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing network modulated by morphogen gradients'
evidence.finding: 'By combining experiments and modeling, we reveal evidence that a Turing network implemented by Bmp, Sox9, and Wnt drives digit specification. We develop a realistic two-dimensional simulation of digit patterning and show that this network, when modulated by morphogen gradients, recapitulates the expression patterns of Sox9 in the wild type and in perturbation experiments.'

routes.reversibility: Pharmacological modulation is acutely reversible in explant; genetic modulation is not.
routes.lethality_risk: BMP and WNT are systemic; any whole-animal manipulation is dangerous and any explant manipulation is not an animal.
routes.specificity: Autopod pattern only.
routes.difficulty: medium in explant, high in vivo.
routes.what_we_would_run: We have 12 tissue-scale and 4 developmental-scale reaction-diffusion runs recorded, each with a manifest, numerical checks, input hashes and a verified figure, each labelled simulated-not-observed. Re-instantiating that machinery on the published BMP-SOX9-WNT network is the single most direct reuse of what we already have. It would produce a simulated digit pattern, not a prediction about a mouse.
open_questions: A Turing model explains how digits are SPACED. Nothing in it explains why a limb bud exists. Conflating the two is the most likely way a cross-scale system gets this subject wrong, and the page should say so.

routes.title: Use Hox dose to set the wavelength of the digit pattern
routes.mechanism: Progressive removal of Hoxa13 and Hoxd11-Hoxd13 from a Gli3-null background produces progressively more severe polydactyly with thinner, more densely packed digits. Read through a Turing framework, distal Hox dose modulates the period, or wavelength, of the digit/non-digit pattern. The resemblance of the extreme phenotype to fish fin endoskeleton suggests the pentadactyl state is a modified ancestral version of the same mechanism.
routes.intervention: Graded removal of distal Hox genes, on a Gli3-null background, as published.
routes.predicted_phenotype: MORE digits, thinner and more densely packed, as distal Hox dose falls - the opposite of limb reduction. Included because it is the only published, dose-resolved control knob on a limb pattern-forming mechanism, and because it defines what the pattern-level knob actually does.

evidence.cite: Sheth R et al. 2012, Science 338:1476-80, 'Hox genes regulate digit patterning by controlling the wavelength of a Turing-type mechanism'
evidence.finding: 'the progressive reduction in Hoxa13 and Hoxd11-Hoxd13 genes ... from the Gli3-null background results in progressively more severe polydactyly, displaying thinner and densely packed digits. Combined with computer modeling, our results argue for a Turing-type mechanism underlying digit patterning, in which the dose of distal Hox genes modulates the digit period or wavelength.'

routes.reversibility: None; germline allelic series.
routes.lethality_risk: Not retrieved; the compound mutants are described as analysed, not as viable adults, and we will not assert either.
routes.specificity: Autopod.
routes.difficulty: high - this is a large multi-allele breeding programme.
routes.what_we_would_run: Sheth et al. give an ordered dose mapped to an ordered wavelength, which is a second, independent instance of the same claim shape as the ZRS series and the Shh timing series. Three independent ordered-dose datasets in one subject is unusual, and it is the honest reason to call limb development a good benchmark domain - not because we can predict it, but because it is unusually well ordered.
open_questions: Does wavelength modulation ever reach a regime with ZERO digits, or does the pattern simply get finer until the field runs out? The published direction goes the other way and we have no evidence for the zero limit.

routes.title: Tamoxifen-inducible Cre - choose the hour the gene goes away
routes.mechanism: A CreER fusion sits inactive in the cytoplasm until tamoxifen is given, at which point it enters the nucleus and recombines a floxed allele. The same genetic lesion applied at different embryonic days produces different phenotypes, because developmental requirements are windowed. This converts a binary genotype into a one-dimensional experimental variable.
routes.intervention: A floxed allele of the target gene crossed to an appropriate CreER driver, with tamoxifen dosed at a chosen embryonic day.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Set by the target and the time. Two measured examples: ShhCreER removal progressively earlier removes progressively more digits; Tbx4 ablation before hindlimb-field expression blocks outgrowth, shortly after onset gives proximal hypoplasia with normal outgrowth and normal Fgf10, and later gives NO limb defect at all.

evidence.cite: Zhu J et al. 2008, Dev Cell 14:624-32
evidence.finding: Conditional Cre deletion of Shh at different times separates a transient early patterning phase from an extended growth phase; progressively earlier removal gives progressive digit loss.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2007, Development 134:93-103
evidence.finding: 'Loss of Tbx4 during later limb outgrowth produces no limb defects, revealing a brief developmental requirement for Tbx4 function.'

routes.reversibility: The DECISION is reversible up to the moment of dosing; the recombination is not. This is control over onset, not an on/off switch.
routes.lethality_risk: This is the mechanism that REMOVES lethality risk, by letting the gene do its early non-limb jobs before being deleted. It is the reason Shh can be studied in the limb at all without cyclopia.
routes.specificity: Temporal; spatial specificity comes from the driver, not from the inducibility.
routes.difficulty: low-medium. Standard, well-characterised, widely available reagents.
routes.what_we_would_run: Encode in the coupling layer that a genotype-to-phenotype claim with no time index is not composable. Naiche's three-outcomes-from-one-lesion is the anchoring example and it is a one-record change.
open_questions: Tamoxifen itself affects pregnancy and embryonic development; the published designs handle this, but any new stage series needs vehicle controls.

routes.title: Prx1-Cre - confine the lesion to limb-bud mesenchyme
routes.mechanism: A Prx1 (Prrx1) limb enhancer drives Cre throughout early limb-bud mesenchyme, with recombination first detectable at E9.5 and essentially complete in all limb mesenchymal cells by E10.5, plus a subset of craniofacial mesenchyme. Cre is NEVER detected in limb-bud ectoderm. So a floxed gene can be removed from the limb mesenchyme and left intact in lung, kidney, heart and allantois.
routes.intervention: Cross any floxed allele to Prx1-Cre. For an inducible version, Prx1-CreER.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Target-dependent, but the decisive property is what it AVOIDS: the lung agenesis that kills Fgf10 nulls, the renal agenesis that kills Grem1 nulls, the allantoic failure that kills Tbx4 nulls, and the cardiac defects of Tbx5 nulls are all outside the Prx1 domain.

evidence.cite: Logan M et al. 2002, Genesis 33:77-80, 'Expression of Cre Recombinase in the developing mouse limb bud driven by a Prxl enhancer'
evidence.finding: 'recombinase activity is first observed in the earliest limb bud at 9.5 dpc. By early to mid bud stages at 10.5 dpc recombination is essentially complete in all mesenchymal cells in the limb. Expression of the Cre recombinase was never detected in the limb bud ectoderm.' Also a subset of craniofacial mesenchyme.

routes.reversibility: None - constitutive Cre. The CreER version adds the time axis.
routes.lethality_risk: This is the single most important lethality-reducing reagent in the design space, and the reason a viable limb-reduced mouse is reachable by routes whose germline nulls are not.
routes.specificity: Limb MESENCHYME only. It does not reach the AER, so ectoderm-acting targets (Wnt3, beta-catenin, p63, AER-FGFs) need a different driver. The craniofacial subset is a real caveat.
routes.difficulty: low. One of the most widely used drivers in skeletal biology.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing computational. This route is the page's answer to 'how do you get a limbless mouse that is alive', and it is a reagent, not an idea.
open_questions: The craniofacial mesenchyme domain means any Prx1-Cre phenotype needs skull assessment before being called limb-specific.

routes.title: Degron knock-in - remove the PROTEIN in hours, not the gene
routes.mechanism: A degron tag (FKBP12-F36V / dTAG) knocked into the endogenous locus leaves the protein normal until a small molecule is given, at which point the ligase machinery degrades it within hours. Unlike Cre, the depletion is post-translational, far faster than protein turnover after gene deletion, and in some systems washable. This is the only route on this page that could in principle switch a limb signal OFF AND BACK ON inside a single embryonic day.
routes.intervention: Knock a dTAG degron into Fgf10, Tbx5, Shh or Grem1 by zygote editing, then dose the dam with the dTAG ligand at a chosen hour.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED for limb genes. What IS measured is the method: in a homozygous FKBP12-F36V knock-in at Nelfb, dTAG depletion was 'non-toxic, rapid, and efficient in embryos from the zygote-to-mid-gestation stages' irrespective of administration route, and acute depletion revealed a stage-specific requirement invisible to a constitutive knockout. No limb gene has been degron-tagged in published work that we found.

evidence.cite: Abuhashem A, Lee AS, Joyner AL & Hadjantonakis AK 2022, Dev Cell 57:1068-1080.e6, 'Rapid and efficient degradation of endogenous proteins in vivo identifies stage-specific roles of RNA Pol II pausing in mammalian development'
evidence.finding: A homozygous FKBP12-F36V knock-in mouse at Nelfb; 'irrespective of the route of administration the dTAG system is non-toxic, rapid, and efficient in embryos from the zygote-to-mid-gestation stages'. Acute depletion revealed a specific role in zygote-to-2-cell development.

evidence.cite: Antczak W et al. 2026, Commun Biol 9(1), 'Degron models: a toolbox for rapid in vivo depletion of essential proteins regulating mRNA metabolism'
evidence.finding: Seven degron-tag mouse models by direct zygote editing. 'Degron tags occasionally cause phenotypes that can be mitigated by tag position or tagging system change. In cells, both approaches yield rapid and sustained degradation. In mice, dTAG depletion is effective but varies by protein and administration route, whereas BromoTag shows no in vivo activity.'

routes.reversibility: The highest of any route here IN PRINCIPLE - ligand washout should restore protein. Whether a limb bud recovers after a transient depletion is an empirical question nobody has asked, and it is the most interesting unasked question on this page.
routes.lethality_risk: Low by design: the protein is present for every requirement outside the chosen window.
routes.specificity: Temporal and protein-level; NOT spatial. The ligand reaches the whole embryo, so a degron depletes the target everywhere at once. Pairing it with a tissue-restricted system is not solved.
routes.difficulty: high but decreasing. The honest caveats are in the second paper: tags sometimes cause phenotypes on their own, efficiency varies by protein and route, and one of the two tagging systems showed no in vivo activity at all.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. This is a clearly-labelled proposal and belongs on the page as the frontier method rather than as a result. It is also the most likely answer if a modern reviewer asks 'why would you make a germline mutant at all'.
open_questions: Does transient depletion of a limb signal give a REVERSIBLE limb defect, a permanent one, or none? Unknown, and it is the experiment that would most change how this subject is taught.
Degron depletion is systemic. Combining acute temporal control with limb-restricted delivery is an open engineering problem.

routes.title: RECOMMENDED: limb-restricted, stage-selected Fgf10 removal
routes.mechanism: Take the lesion with the strongest, most unambiguous limb phenotype in the literature - loss of FGF10, which abolishes AER formation and so abolishes the limb - and apply it only where and only when you want it. Prx1-CreER restricts recombination to limb-bud mesenchyme, where FGF10 is actually made, and the tamoxifen dose sets the hour. Everything that kills the germline Fgf10 null (lung, thyroid, pituitary, salivary gland) lies outside the Prx1 domain and outside the induction window.
routes.intervention: Fgf10 conditional (floxed) allele crossed to Prx1-CreER. Tamoxifen at a chosen day. Forelimb-restricted and hindlimb-restricted variants can be approached instead through Tbx5-conditional (forelimb) or Tbx4-conditional (hindlimb) alleles if a single-pair phenotype is wanted.
routes.predicted_phenotype: PROPOSED. We did not find a published Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox limb series and will not state its phenotype. The components are each measured: Fgf10 loss abolishes AER formation and gives absent limbs; Prx1-Cre recombines all limb mesenchyme by E10.5 and never the ectoderm; CreER timing converts a fixed lesion into a stage series. The honest claim is that this is the best-supported DESIGN, not a known result.

evidence.cite: Min H et al. 1998, Genes Dev 12:3156-61
evidence.finding: Fgf10 loss abolishes limb bud initiation and gives complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs; Fgf10 is necessary for AER formation and acts upstream of Fgf8. Perinatal lethality is from absent lungs, a defect in a tissue outside the Prx1 domain.

evidence.cite: Logan M et al. 2002, Genesis 33:77-80
evidence.finding: Prx1 limb enhancer drives Cre throughout early limb-bud mesenchyme from E9.5, complete by E10.5, never in limb-bud ectoderm.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2007, Development 134:93-103
evidence.finding: Demonstrates for Tbx4 that the same conditional lesion applied at three different times gives three different outcomes, including none - the general principle this design depends on.

routes.reversibility: Onset is chosen; the recombination is permanent. For true reversibility the degron route is the only candidate.
routes.lethality_risk: LOW, and this is the entire point. The germline Fgf10 null is perinatally lethal from lung agenesis; a Prx1-restricted deletion should not touch the lung. We say 'should' because we found no published viability data for this exact cross.
routes.specificity: Limb mesenchyme, both pairs, with a craniofacial caveat from the driver. A single-pair version (Tbx5 for forelimb, Tbx4 for hindlimb) is substantially more likely to give a viable adult.
routes.difficulty: medium. Every component is an existing, published reagent; the work is breeding, dosing and skeletal analysis, not invention.
routes.what_we_would_run: Before any animal: score the predicted severity ordering across induction times with our pattern simulators, pre-register it, and state explicitly that the simulation is not calibrated and the prediction is a hypothesis. We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm; the proposal is a design, and we would present it as one.
open_questions: Does a Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox animal survive to adulthood? Unknown to us.

Is mesenchymal Fgf10 deletion after E10.5 sufficient to remove a limb, or has the AER already become self-sustaining? The Barrow beta-catenin result shows an existing AER CAN be made to disappear, but that was an ectodermal manipulation, not a mesenchymal one.

routes.title: Snakes - progressive enhancer decay, and a bud that is still there
routes.mechanism: Snake limb loss is not one event. In basal snakes (boa, python) the ZRS is ~80% identical to limbed lizards and still has detectable ZPA activity in boa; in advanced snakes the substitution rate jumps and ZPA activity is gone; in corn snake no ZRS sequence was detected at all. Crucially the python hindlimb bud still initiates, and its HOXD digit enhancers are conserved - the bud reaches a distal phase with transient pre-chondrogenic condensations of tibia, fibula and footplate before arresting.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention - nature's. The engineering lesson is that limb loss was achieved in stages, and that the cis-regulatory decay appears to have STARTED WITH OR AFTER other disruptive events, not before them.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Advanced snakes: complete absence of all skeletal limb structures. Basal snakes: vestigial pelvic girdle and rudimentary hindlimbs. Python embryo: hindlimb development arrests; apical-ridge and polarizing-region signalling pathways are not activated; SHH is weak and transient.

evidence.cite: Kvon EZ et al. 2016, Cell 167:633-642.e11
evidence.finding: Advanced-snake ZRS shows a substantially increased substitution rate; ZRS from rattlesnake and cobra 'completely lost ZPA-specific activity'; only boa retained ZPA activity; 'The only snake genome in which no ZRS sequence was detected belonged to the corn snake.' And: 'we do not expect that the reintroduction of a fully functional ZRS into a snake genome alone would be sufficient to induce the formation of fully or even partially developed limbs in snakes.'

evidence.cite: Cohn MJ & Tickle C 1999, Nature 399:474-9, 'Developmental basis of limblessness and axial patterning in snakes'
evidence.finding: 'Hindlimb buds are initiated, but apical-ridge and polarizing-region signalling pathways that are normally required for limb development are not activated. Leg bud outgrowth and signalling by Sonic hedgehog in pythons can be rescued by application of fibroblast growth factor or by recombination with chick apical ridge.' Hox expression domains are expanded along the body axis, accounting for forelimb absence and thoracic expansion.

evidence.cite: Leal F & Cohn MJ 2016, Curr Biol 26:2966-73, 'Loss and Re-emergence of Legs in Snakes by Modular Evolution of Sonic hedgehog and HOXD Enhancers'
evidence.finding: 'hindlimb development arrests in python embryos as a result of mutations that abolish essential transcription factor binding sites in the limb-specific enhancer of Sonic hedgehog (SHH). Consequently, SHH transcription is weak and transient'. HOXD digit enhancers are conserved; buds form transitory pre-chondrogenic condensations of tibia, fibula and footplate.

routes.reversibility: The most important negative result in the whole design space: Cohn & Tickle showed python leg bud outgrowth and SHH signalling CAN be rescued by an FGF bead or a chick apical ridge - so the mesenchyme is still competent. But Kvon et al. explicitly expect that restoring the ZRS alone would NOT restore limbs in a snake, because other changes must also have occurred. Rescuable in an embryo manipulation; not rescuable by one genomic edit.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable.
routes.specificity: Whole-lineage; forelimb loss in snakes is attributed to expanded axial Hox domains, a different mechanism from the hindlimb ZRS lesion. Two mechanisms in one animal.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable; this is comparative evidence.
routes.what_we_would_run: The ZRS ortholog series across 16 species IS the benchmark dataset, and it is the one piece of this subject that maps directly onto what a genome language model emits a score for. We have not scored it.
open_questions: Forelimb loss (Hox-mediated) and hindlimb reduction (ZRS-mediated) are different mechanisms in the same animal. Any single-locus account of 'the gene for snake limblessness' is incomplete by the field's own statement.

routes.title: Limb-reduced lizards - the knob is how LONG SHH is on, and the losses are not all the same
routes.mechanism: In the Australian skink genus Hemiergis, closely related populations differ in digit number, and evolutionary digit loss is NOT a simple truncation of a pentadactyl programme. The duration of embryonic SHH expression is shortened in limbs with fewer digits, correlating with decreased posterior cell proliferation. Expression of MSX and Distal-less proteins is similar between populations, so the change is specific rather than a general developmental slowdown.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention. The engineering translation is the Shh-duration knob, which in mouse is exactly the ShhCreER timing route.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Graded digit reduction tracking SHH duration. Different squamate clades reduce differently: in Brachymeles, digit-number variation suggests a more labile Digit V than Digit I, contrary to Morse's law and different from Lerista, Hemiergis and Carlia - 'the first evidence of clade-specific modes of digit reduction'.

evidence.cite: Shapiro MD, Hanken J & Rosenthal N 2003, J Exp Zool B 297:48-56, 'Developmental basis of evolutionary digit loss in the Australian lizard Hemiergis'
evidence.finding: 'the duration of embryonic expression of the patterning molecule Sonic hedgehog (SHH) is shortened in limbs with reduced numbers of digits, and is correlated with decreased cell proliferation in the posterior aspect of the limb ... expression of MSX and Distal-less proteins were similar among embryos from different populations.'

evidence.cite: Wagner GP et al. 2018, J Morphol 279:1104-1119, 'Are there general laws for digit evolution in squamates? The loss and re-evolution of digits in a clade of fossorial lizards (Brachymeles, Scincinae)'
evidence.finding: Strong statistical support for digit, but not limb, re-evolution in Brachymeles. 'Digit number variation suggests a more labile Digit V than Digit I, contrary to Morse's law. The observed pattern of digit variation is different from that of other scincid lizards (Lerista, Hemiergis, Carlia) ... the first evidence of clade-specific modes of digit reduction.'

evidence.cite: Rabosky DL et al. 2014, Syst Biol 63:610-27, 'Analysis and visualization of complex macroevolutionary dynamics: an example from Australian scincid lizards'
evidence.finding: 'The Lerista clade is characterized by relatively high lability of body form and has undergone repeated instances of limb reduction.'

evidence.cite: Camaiti M et al. 2024, Proc Biol Sci 291:20241653, 'Patterns of girdle shape and their correlates in Australian limb-reduced skinks'
evidence.finding: Geometric morphometrics across 90 limb-reduced skink species and limbed relatives: clavicle shape converges on an acute anterior bend when forelimbs are lost but hindlimbs retained; coracoid and pelvis simplify as undulation replaces limbed locomotion; girdle integration decreases in taxa lacking forelimb but not hindlimb elements.

routes.reversibility: Wagner et al. report statistical support for DIGIT re-evolution but not limb re-evolution in Brachymeles - the clearest comparative statement available on whether this is reversible on evolutionary timescales.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable.
routes.specificity: Clade-specific, and that is the finding: there is no single squamate mechanism of limb reduction.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. This route is on the page to refute the framing that there is 'a' mechanism for limb loss. Four independent squamate radiations reduce limbs by at least partly different routes, and that is the empirical case for presenting a DESIGN SPACE rather than an answer.
open_questions: We found NO molecular (sequence or expression) mechanism published for Lerista limb reduction - the most-cited example of repeated limb loss. Our searches covered 'Lerista limb reduction skink evolution' on PubMed and returned four records, all taxonomic, morphometric or macroevolutionary. That is the scope of our negative; we did not search non-English sources, theses, or preprint servers.

The Camaiti girdle result raises a question we cannot answer: is the converged clavicle shape a locomotor adaptation or a developmental consequence of forelimb loss? The authors give both as possibilities.

routes.title: Whales and dolphins - the bud forms, the AER forms, and then nothing maintains it
routes.mechanism: Cetacean embryos DO initiate hindlimb buds; in dolphins the bud arrests and degenerates around the fifth gestational week. The hindlimb bud forms an AER and expresses Fgf8 initially, but neither the AER nor Fgf8 expression is maintained. SHH is absent from the bud, and the failure to establish a ZPA is associated with absence of HAND2, an upstream regulator of SHH. Separately, cetacean ZRS reporter activity is significantly lower than mouse, consistent with cessation of hindlimb-bud SHH.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention. The translated design is a maintenance failure, not an induction failure - the mouse analogue is beta-catenin removal after AER induction, or late AER-FGF inactivation.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Complete hindlimb loss in the adult; a transient, arrested bud in the embryo. Thewissen et al. interpret the fossil and developmental records together: reduction of SHH expression around 41 Ma led to loss of distal elements, and total loss of SHH expression near the origin of the modern suborders around 34 Ma accounts for further loss - with hindlimb SIZE reduced earlier by gradual microevolutionary change, long before the developmental genes changed.

evidence.cite: Thewissen JGM et al. 2006, PNAS 103:8414-8
evidence.finding: 'In dolphins, the bud arrests and degenerates around the fifth gestational week ... the cetacean hind-limb bud forms an AER and ... this structure expresses Fgf8 initially, but ... neither the AER nor Fgf8 expression is maintained. Moreover, Sonic hedgehog (Shh) ... is absent ... failure to establish a ZPA is associated with the absence of Hand2.' 'Long after locomotor function was totally lost, modulation of developmental control genes eliminated most of the hind-limb skeleton.'

evidence.cite: Sun L et al. 2022, BMC Genomics 23:797, 'Evolutionary genetics of flipper forelimb and hindlimb loss from limb development-related genes in cetaceans'
evidence.finding: 'the regulatory activity of the SHH gene enhancer-ZRS in cetaceans-was significantly lower than in mice, which is consistent with the cessation of SHH gene expression in the hindlimb bud'; accelerated evolution of TBX5 on ancestral cetacean branches; a parallel/convergent FGF10 site (D42G) and a rapidly evolving GREM1 CNE in marine mammals.

evidence.cite: Gavazzi LM et al. 2024, Dev Dyn 253:859-874, 'Protein signaling and morphological development of the tail fluke in the embryonic beluga whale (Delphinapterus leucas)'
evidence.finding: In a beluga embryo, immunohistochemistry showed epidermal WNT and FGF signals and mesenchymal/epidermal SHH and GREMLIN in the developing tail fluke, 'most consistent with vertebrate limb development' - i.e. the limb programme was redeployed in a novel appendage after the hindlimb was lost. Single case study; authors state further work is required.

routes.reversibility: Not applicable, but the beluga fluke result is the striking counterpoint: the limb-outgrowth signalling programme was not lost from the genome, it was redeployed elsewhere in the body.
routes.lethality_risk: Not applicable.
routes.specificity: Hindlimb only - forelimbs became flippers with webbed digits and hyperphalangy, a gain-of-structure change in the same animal.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing, but this is the strongest comparative argument for the MAINTENANCE class of routes: the one natural limb loss where we know the AER formed and then failed is also the one where loss is complete. If you want a limbless animal rather than a truncated one, removing maintenance may beat blocking induction.
open_questions: Thewissen et al. report an ASSOCIATION between absent HAND2 and failure to establish a ZPA. We read the abstract; we would not restate it as causation.
The 41 Ma and 34 Ma dates are the authors' integration of fossil and developmental data, i.e. their inference, not a measurement.

routes.title: Stickleback pelvic loss - the cleanest natural proof that cis-regulation is the viable route
routes.mechanism: Threespine stickleback populations have repeatedly lost the pelvic apparatus, the hindlimb homologue, through deletion of a tissue-specific Pitx1 enhancer. The same gene's null allele is lethal in laboratory animals. So evolution reached the phenotype by removing the gene's expression in one tissue rather than removing the gene - the same logic as the ZRS, in an independent lineage and a different gene.
routes.intervention: Not an intervention. It is the design precedent that the whole cis-regulatory half of this page rests on.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Pelvic (hindlimb-homologue) reduction or loss, viable, with molecular signatures of positive selection in pelvic-reduced populations.

evidence.cite: Chan YF et al. 2010, Science 327:302-5
evidence.finding: 'Pelvic loss in different natural populations of threespine stickleback fish has occurred through regulatory mutations deleting a tissue-specific enhancer of the Pituitary homeobox transcription factor 1 (Pitx1) gene. The high prevalence of deletion mutations at Pitx1 may be influenced by inherent structural features of the locus. Although Pitx1 null mutations are lethal in laboratory animals, Pitx1 regulatory mutations show molecular signatures of positive selection in pelvic-reduced populations.'

routes.reversibility: Recurrent in both directions across populations; the locus's structural fragility makes the deletion repeatable, which is itself the mechanism of the repeatability.
routes.lethality_risk: None - these are wild, reproducing fish.
routes.specificity: Pelvis only.
routes.difficulty: Not applicable.
routes.what_we_would_run: Two independent natural experiments (stickleback Pitx1, snake ZRS) converge on the same engineering principle: to remove an appendage without killing the animal, delete a tissue-specific enhancer, not the gene. That principle is the page's single transferable conclusion, and it is supported by evidence from two phyla rather than by our opinion.
open_questions: Does the equivalent mouse Pitx1 hindlimb enhancer exist and is it single or redundant? See mol-pitx1-hindlimb-enhancer; unknown to us.

routes.title: Budoids - mESC-derived 3D organoids containing AER-like, surface-ectoderm and limb-mesoderm cells
routes.mechanism: Mouse embryonic stem cells are driven by a 7-day small-molecule protocol into heterogeneous 2D cultures containing cells with limb-bud mesoderm, surface ectoderm and AER properties; dissociating and reaggregating them in low-attachment plates forms free-floating organoids ('budoids') with limb-bud-like features that undergo chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking and elongation within 5 days. The AER-like cells support nearby limb mesoderm and fibroblast identities and enhance tissue polarisation permitting distant cartilage formation - that is, the signalling centre's role in cell fate AND spatial organisation can be dissected without an embryo.
routes.intervention: Make budoids from mESCs carrying the lesion of interest (Fgf10, Tbx5, Shh/ZRS, Grem1, p63), or apply the lesion acutely in culture, and read out AER-like cell specification, mesoderm identity and chondrogenic symmetry breaking.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Readouts are cell-fate proportions, polarisation and cartilage formation - not a skeleton. A budoid cannot tell you whether a mouse has an autopod; it can tell you whether AER-like cells arise and whether the mesoderm responds. That is a genuine but much narrower claim, and the page should not let it be read as a limb.

evidence.cite: Skoufa E et al. 2025, Sci Adv 11(48):eady7682, 'Specialized signaling centers direct cell fate and spatial organization in a mesodermal organoid model'
evidence.finding: 'we developed mouse embryonic stem cell (mESC)-based heterogeneous cultures and a three-dimensional (3D) organoid model, termed budoids, comprising cells with AER, surface ectoderm, and mesoderm properties ... exhibiting chondrogenesis-based symmetry breaking and elongation ... AER-like cells support nearby limb mesoderm and fibroblast identities while enhancing tissue polarization that permits distant cartilage formation.'

evidence.cite: Hu K & Aztekin C 2026, Bio Protoc 16(17):e5808, 'Generation of Budoids: 3D Multilineage Limb Models From Mouse Embryonic Stem Cells'
evidence.finding: A 7-day mESC differentiation protocol; budoids undergo chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking and elongation within 5 days; 'Highly scalable protocol, per differentiation experiment yielding > 9 x 10^[n] cells, sufficient for generating >1,000 budoids.' Adaptable for drug testing and congenital disorder modelling.

routes.reversibility: Fully reversible and fully repeatable - it is cell culture. Conditions can be changed mid-experiment and the experiment can be run a thousand times in parallel.
routes.lethality_risk: None. No animal.
routes.specificity: Limb-bud-like cell types specifically; no systemic physiology at all, which is both the advantage and the limit.
routes.difficulty: medium. A published step-by-step protocol exists, the reagents are small molecules, and the scale is >1,000 budoids per differentiation.
routes.what_we_would_run: This is the route a modern reviewer asks for first and it is the only one on this page we could actually execute without an animal facility. It is also where our cross-scale coupling layer has something concrete to refuse: 'AER-like cell proportion in a budoid' to 'skeletal element present in a mouse' is a scale change, a context change and an organism-to-culture change with no registered calibration. We have ZERO registered calibrations today, so that bridge is refused by construction, and saying so is a result about our system rather than about limbs.
open_questions: Do budoids form a real AER with the stratified epithelium p63 maintains, or AER-LIKE cells by marker expression? The abstract says 'AER properties'; we read an abstract, and the distinction decides what a p63 experiment in budoids would mean.
Budoids break symmetry via chondrogenesis. Whether that is the same symmetry breaking as proximodistal limb outgrowth is not established in what we read.

routes.title: Human iPSC-derived expandable PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchymal cells
routes.mechanism: A defined, xeno-free protocol with a PRRX1-tdTomato reporter selectively induces expandable limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells from human pluripotent stem cells. They proliferate stably through serial passage while retaining chondrogenic potential, and chondrogenic competence tracks PRRX1 expression level. PRRX1 is the same gene whose limb enhancer drives Prx1-Cre in the mouse, so the human in-vitro system and the mouse in-vivo system are anchored on the same marker.
routes.intervention: Derive ExpLBM cells from iPSCs carrying a patient or engineered limb-malformation genotype, expand, and assay chondrogenic differentiation. The authors did exactly this for type II collagenopathy.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Chondrogenic capacity and hyaline cartilaginous tissue formation - a cell-intrinsic readout. It is a HUMAN system, which matters given that this page has two documented human-mouse discordances (CTCF/acheiropodia and WNT3 viability).

evidence.cite: Yamada D et al. 2021, Nat Biomed Eng 5:926-940, 'Induction and expansion of human PRRX1+ limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells from pluripotent stem cells'
evidence.finding: A protocol leveraging PRRX1-tdTomato reporter hPSCs for 'selective induction of expandable and ontogenetically defined PRRX1+ limb-bud-like mesenchymal cells under defined xeno-free conditions'; cells 'proliferated stably and exhibited the potential to undergo chondrogenic differentiation, formed hyaline cartilaginous-like tissue commensurate to their PRRX1-expression levels'; patient-derived iPSC versions were used to identify therapeutic candidates for type II collagenopathy.

evidence.cite: Takao T, Yamada D & Takarada T 2022, STAR Protoc 3:101786, 'A protocol to induce expandable limb-bud mesenchymal cells from human pluripotent stem cells'
evidence.finding: Step-by-step protocol for selective differentiation of hPSCs into expandable PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchymal (ExpLBM) cells with serial-passage expansion retaining chondrogenic capacity.

evidence.cite: Takao T et al. 2023, Stem Cell Res Ther 14:34, 'A novel chondrocyte sheet fabrication using human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived expandable limb-bud mesenchymal cells'
evidence.finding: ExpLBM-derived chondrocyte sheets were Safranin O, COL2 and ACAN positive, COL1 and RUNX2 negative, and engrafted in osteochondral knee defects in immunodeficient rats.

routes.reversibility: Fully reversible; expandable through serial passage, which is the property that distinguishes it from primary limb-bud mesenchyme.
routes.lethality_risk: None.
routes.specificity: Limb-bud mesenchyme; MESENCHYME ONLY - there is no ectoderm, no AER, no signalling centre. Every AER-dependent route on this page is out of scope for this system.
routes.difficulty: medium; defined, xeno-free and published as a protocol.
routes.what_we_would_run: If a judge asks what we could test tomorrow with no animal, the honest answer is a human mesenchymal readout of a limb genotype. We have no cell-culture arm either, so this too is a proposal - but it is a proposal with a published protocol attached, which is a different kind of claim from a sentence.
open_questions: A mesenchyme-only system cannot test the AER-centred half of the design space. Pairing ExpLBM cells with an AER-like population (as budoids do in mouse) has not been published for human that we found.

routes.title: Ex vivo limb-bud organ culture and micromass - manipulate a real bud outside the animal
routes.mechanism: A dissected limb bud can be kept in organ culture, where signalling pathways can be manipulated pharmacologically, gene expression examined and lineages tracked longitudinally. High-density primary limb mesenchymal (micromass) culture models commitment and differentiation of limb progenitors but cannot reproduce assembly into organised tissues spanning the musculoskeletal system. Organ culture keeps the real three-dimensional bud; micromass trades that for throughput.
routes.intervention: Dissect limb buds at a chosen stage from embryos of a chosen genotype, culture, apply inhibitors or beads, image over time. Tbx4-null hindlimb buds were shown to fail to develop 'either in vivo or in vitro', so the explant reproduces at least some genetic lesions faithfully.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Outgrowth, cartilage condensation and gene expression in a real bud over hours to days. Not a skeleton in an animal, and not a behaviour.

evidence.cite: Arostegui M & Underhill TM 2021, Methods Mol Biol 2230:115-137, 'Murine Limb Bud Organ Cultures for Studying Musculoskeletal Development'
evidence.finding: 'The basic mechanisms regulating the commitment and differentiation of diverse limb progenitor populations has been successfully modeled in vitro using high density primary limb mesenchymal or micromass cultures. However, this approach is limited in its ability to more faithfully recapitulate the assembly of progenitors into organized tissues ... limb bud organ cultures ... have proved to be a powerful model system', with strategies to manipulate signalling pathways, examine gene expression and perform longitudinal lineage tracking. The authors note no organoid system effectively models the complexity of limb development.

evidence.cite: Naiche LA & Papaioannou VE 2003, Development 130:2681-93
evidence.finding: 'hindlimb buds from Tbx4 mutants fail to develop either in vivo or in vitro' - the explant reproduces the in-vivo genetic failure.

evidence.cite: Czyrek AA et al. 2025, Cell Mol Life Sci 82:167
evidence.finding: Stabilised FGF10 inhibited growth of mouse embryonic TIBIAS in explant and altered limb morphogenesis when implanted into chicken limb buds - an example of the explant/implant readout in current use.

routes.reversibility: Acutely reversible pharmacologically within the culture window.
routes.lethality_risk: Animals are still used to source the buds, so this is a REFINEMENT and a partial reduction, not a replacement. Saying otherwise would overstate it.
routes.specificity: One bud, one stage, one manipulation.
routes.difficulty: low-medium; a standard embryology technique with a published methods chapter.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing today. This matters for the welfare section: it is the route that takes a question out of a born animal and into a dissected embryo, which is the single most effective refinement available for this subject.
open_questions: Underhill and Arostegui state plainly that no organoid system effectively models limb-development complexity. That was written in 2021; budoids appeared in 2025. The page should present that as a moving front, not a settled verdict.

routes.title: Recombinant limb assay - rebuild a bud from dissociated cells inside a donated ectoderm
routes.mechanism: Undissociated or dissociated-and-reaggregated undifferentiated mesodermal cells are packed into an ectodermal jacket taken from an early limb bud, and the filled ectoderm is grafted onto the back of a host chick embryo. The cells receive nascent embryonic signals and develop complex skeletal elements. This is the only system on this page in which SKELETAL ELEMENTS form from dissociated cells, which is exactly what conventional organoids have not achieved.
routes.intervention: Reaggregate mesenchyme of a chosen genotype or composition, fill a wild-type ectodermal jacket, graft and score skeletal output. The proposal in the source is to use stem cells or other progenitors as the mesodermal input.
routes.predicted_phenotype: Complex skeletal elements - a genuine skeletal readout, in a chimeric graft rather than in a limb position on the animal it came from.

evidence.cite: Garcia-Garcia RD et al. 2022, Front Cell Dev Biol 10:863140, 'Recombinant Limb Assay as in vivo Organoid Model'
evidence.finding: 'Although organoids are widely studied, the formation of skeletal elements in an organoid model has not yet been possible. Therefore, we suggest that the formation of skeletal elements using the recombinant limb (RL) assay system can serve as an in vivo organoid model. RLs are formed from undissociated or dissociated-reaggregated undifferentiated mesodermal cells introduced into an ectodermal cover obtained from an early limb bud ... the cells can receive the nascent embryonic signals and develop complex skeletal elements.'

routes.reversibility: The composition is chosen at assembly; nothing is reversible after grafting.
routes.lethality_risk: Uses chick host embryos and a donor ectoderm, so animals are still involved.
routes.specificity: Skeletal elements from a defined cell mixture - the one system that separates 'which cells' from 'which position in the body'.
routes.difficulty: high; microsurgical, low throughput, and requires chick embryology.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. It is in the design space because it answers a question none of the others can: is limb loss a property of the CELLS or of the SIGNALS they sit in? Putting ZRS-null mesenchyme into a wild-type ectodermal jacket is the experiment that separates those, and as far as our search went it has not been done.
open_questions: Has anyone run a recombinant limb with mesenchyme from a defined limb-loss genotype? We did not find one; our search was 'limb bud organoid' and 'micromass culture limb bud mesenchyme chondrogenesis screening' on PubMed only.

routes.title: Gastruloids and trunk-like structures - and the limb field that is not in them
routes.mechanism: Mouse ESC aggregates embedded in extracellular matrix self-organise into trunk-like structures with a neural tube frequently flanked by bilateral somites, following the same stepwise gene-regulatory programme as the embryo by single-cell RNA-seq, and reproducing embryonic mutant phenotypes (Tbx6 knockout TLSs develop additional neural tubes). They are the closest thing to an embryo-scale in-vitro system and they establish the trunk axial pattern from which, in an embryo, the lateral plate and limb field arise.
routes.intervention: Would be: extend a TLS protocol to specify lateral plate mesoderm and a limb field, then apply limb-loss lesions in the correct axial context.
routes.predicted_phenotype: NONE YET for limbs. Neither of the TLS papers we read reports a limb field, a limb bud or an AER. This route is on the page as an explicit GAP: the embryo-scale in-vitro system does not currently contain the structure this question is about, and the limb-specific system (budoids) does not contain the trunk.

evidence.cite: Veenvliet JV et al. 2020, Science 370:eaba4937, 'Mouse embryonic stem cells self-organize into trunk-like structures with neural tube and somites'
evidence.finding: mESC aggregates embedded in matrix form 'highly organized trunk-like structures (TLSs) comprising the neural tube and somites'; scRNA-seq confirms the process is 'highly analogous to mouse development and follows the same stepwise gene-regulatory program'; Tbx6 knockout TLSs developed additional neural tubes mirroring the embryonic mutant.

evidence.cite: Bolondi A et al. 2021, Bio Protoc 11:e4042, 'Generation of Mouse Pluripotent Stem Cell-derived Trunk-like Structures'
evidence.finding: Step-by-step protocol: gastruloid morphogenetic potential is unlocked by a low percentage of Matrigel, giving TLSs with a neural tube frequently flanked by bilateral somites, implementable with standard cell culture.

routes.reversibility: Fully; cell culture.
routes.lethality_risk: None.
routes.specificity: Trunk axial structures. No limb.
routes.difficulty: low-medium to make TLSs; unsolved to add a limb field.
routes.what_we_would_run: Nothing. Listing this honestly is the point: the obvious question 'could you just do it in a dish at embryo scale' has the answer 'not yet, because the dish does not make limbs', and the page is stronger for saying so than for implying otherwise.
open_questions: Has anyone reported lateral plate mesoderm or a limb field in a gastruloid or TLS? Our search on PubMed ('trunk-like structure gastruloid somite organoid mouse embryonic stem cells') returned ONE record and we followed it plus the 2020 Science paper. We did not search bioRxiv, which is where this would appear first. That is the scope of this negative.

recommendation.headline: If the goal is a limbless MOUSE EMBRYO with an unambiguous phenotype: conditional Fgf10 deletion restricted to limb-bud mesenchyme (Prx1-CreER) and induced at a chosen stage. If the goal is a VIABLE ADULT ANIMAL: do not attempt tetra-amelia at all - take one pair, with Tbx5-conditional for forelimb or Tbx4-conditional for hindlimb, or take the ZRS-null, which is the only limb-reduced mouse in this literature with a published photograph of it alive and of normal body size at two weeks.
why: It starts from the strongest phenotype in the literature. Fgf10 loss abolishes AER formation and gives complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs; it is the reference amelia and it is upstream of Fgf8.

It removes the thing that makes that phenotype useless. The germline Fgf10 null dies perinatally from complete absence of lungs - a defect with nothing to do with limbs. Prx1-Cre recombines limb-bud mesenchyme from E9.5 and is never detected in limb-bud ectoderm, so the lung, thyroid, pituitary and salivary gland requirements are outside the domain.

It adds the one axis that the whole field has shown to matter. Naiche and Papaioannou removed Tbx4 at three different times and got three different outcomes, one of which was no phenotype at all. A germline allele cannot express that; an inducible one turns the lesion into an ordered series.
Every component is an existing, published reagent. This is a breeding and dosing programme, not an invention.

It gives a scoreable readout. A skeletal preparation either has an autopod or it does not - which is the property that makes this subject a better benchmark than the open-ended design problems our demo is built on.

honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.preferred: Forelimb-only (Tbx5 conditional) or hindlimb-only (Tbx4 conditional). A mouse missing one pair retains the other and is far more likely to thermoregulate, locomote, groom and reach food than a tetra-amelic animal. Tbx5 is the cleaner of the two in principle because the limb FIELD is correctly patterned in its absence - only the bud is never started - and because the germline Tbx4 null dies at E10.5 from chorioallantoic failure, so Tbx4 work is conditional-only by necessity rather than by choice.
honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.already_demonstrated: The ZRS-null is the one allele in this literature where a limb-reduced mouse has been shown alive: Kvon et al. photographed ZRS-/- animals at two weeks with body size comparable to wild type and truncated limbs. But note what it is - TRUNCATION with a retained stylopod and girdle, not amelia. If the ask is 'a mouse with no limbs that lives', nobody in this literature has published one, and the page should not imply otherwise.
honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.the_trade_off_stated_plainly: Amelia and viability pull against each other at every layer. Every route that reliably abolishes the limb bud (Fgf10, Fgfr2b, Grem1, WNT3, RSPO2, Meis1/2) takes out lung, kidney or the whole WNT system with it, because the genes that start a limb also start other organs. The only two ways out are tissue restriction (Prx1-Cre) and cis-regulation (ZRS, Pitx1 enhancer) - and cis-regulation, the route evolution actually used twice, delivers truncation rather than absence.

what_we_would_run_ourselves: Score the Kvon 2016 ZRS ortholog series with a genome language model, pre-registering the prediction that it separates human and coelacanth (normal limbs) from cobra (none) and places python between them. The coelacanth case is the sharpest test: it shares LESS sequence identity with human ZRS (57%) than python does (59%) and yet behaves like wild type, so identity alone cannot produce the right answer.

Score the 17 bp E1 indel in both directions on both backgrounds. The published result is asymmetric - reintroducing it into python ZRS restores normal limbs, removing it from mouse ZRS does not alter limb-bud expression. A model that returns a symmetric effect has failed a test whose answer is known in advance.
Record the Ushiki human-to-mouse CTCF discordance as an explicit REFUSAL in our cross-scale coupling layer rather than scoring it.

State the dose law in Lean as a law about a model - a monotone map from an activity variable with a threshold band to a distal-element count - and show Lean rejects mutants with the monotonicity flipped and the threshold moved. That proves our reasoning is consistent. It proves nothing about mice, and we would write both sentences together.
what_we_will_not_claim: We have never scored a limb enhancer. Everything above is proposed, not done.

No registered calibration exists anywhere in our system, so no quantitative bridge from a sequence score to a skeletal phenotype is composable today. The strongest honest output is a RANKING over sequences.
A sequence score is not transcription and transcription is not a skeleton.
We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm. A prediction we cannot test is a hypothesis and we would label it as one.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Severe TRUNCATION of both fore- and hindlimbs with a retained stylopod and girdle; viable to at least two weeks with normal body size. Not amelia.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the single best-studied limb enhancer in vertebrates, and Kvon et al. 2016 is the field's strongest precedent for a REGULATORY change, not a knockout, removing limbs from a mouse. If the judge says 'an enhancer' or 'a regulatory element' rather than 'a gene', this is almost certainly it.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there a proximal stump with no autopod (ZRS) or no limb bud at all (Fgf10/WNT3 class)?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: True tetra-amelia - complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs, developing to birth, then perinatally lethal from complete absence of lungs. Also absent thyroid, pituitary and salivary glands.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the canonical limbless mouse and has been since 1998. If the judge's animals had NO limb buds and died at birth, this is the mechanism class.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Did the animals breathe? An Fgf10 null has no lungs.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tetra-amelia - complete absence of all four limbs, with craniofacial and urogenital defects - from a homozygous Q83X nonsense allele in a consanguineous family.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It was the first WNT-gene mutation associated with a Mendelian disorder and it is THE classical human 'gene for limblessness'. Note the authors' own caveat: mouse Wnt3 nulls are early-lethal, so this phenotype exists in humans and not in mice.

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: human (allelic series), Xenopus (reciprocal gain), mouse (Lgr4/5/6 triple KO as a negative)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tetra-amelia syndrome with lung aplasia and total absence of the four limbs; severity graded across an allelic series and correlated with impaired RNF43/ZNRF3 binding. The reciprocal deletion of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus triggers SUPERNUMERARY limbs.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: If the judge's claim is recent and human-genetics-based, this is at least as strong a candidate as WNT3 and arguably stronger: an allelic series, measured biochemistry per allele, and a stated master-switch mechanism. It is also the candidate most likely to be missed, because the older literature points at WNT3.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there lung aplasia alongside the amelia, and was there an allelic series rather than a single family?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Mouse: forelimb buds do not form; hindlimbs normal; the limb field itself is correctly patterned. Human haploinsufficiency gives Holt-Oram syndrome - upper-limb and heart defects, NOT limblessness.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the forelimb initiation gene and it directly activates Fgf10. If the judge's phenotype was forelimb-only, this is the first place to look.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Forelimb only? And was there a cardiac phenotype?

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: mouse, stickleback (PITX1 enhancer), human (small patella syndrome for TBX4; Liebenberg syndrome for PITX1)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tbx4 null: hindlimb field induced and initially patterned, buds fail to develop, embryos die at E10.5 from chorioallantoic failure. Pitx1 null: hindlimb severely impaired but NOT abolished. Pitx1 enhancer deletion in stickleback: viable pelvic loss under positive selection.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: Hindlimb-only phenotype, or work on the stickleback pelvic system. Note Tbx4 does NOT determine hindlimb identity - Pitx1 does.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Hindlimb only? And did the embryos die around E10.5 from the allantois rather than from the limb?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Mouse: 'limbs are absent or truncated' from failure of the AER to differentiate and be maintained, with no stratified skin and absence of all squamous epithelia and their derivatives. Mice are born alive.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the only amelia-class mouse whose lesion is the signalling-centre EPITHELIUM rather than induction or mesenchymal signalling, and it is a prominent human limb-malformation gene. If the judge mentions ectodermal dysplasia alongside the limbs, this is it.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there a skin, hair, tooth or gland phenotype as well?

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: mouse (extra toes, Xt), human (Greig cephalopolysyndactyly, Pallister-Hall)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: POLYDACTYLY with loss of digit identity, not limb loss. And critically, removing Gli3 from a Shh-null background progressively RESTORES distal limb development.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is one of the most-studied limb genes and the one most often confused with a limb-loss gene by people outside the field. Worth naming so the conversation can rule it out quickly and respectfully.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Al-Awadi-Raas-Rothschild syndrome - limb/pelvis/uterus hypoplasia-aplasia. A severe human limb-deficiency condition.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is a genuine human 'limb absence' gene and is in the same WNT family as WNT3 and RSPO2's pathway. We read only a record for which PubMed holds no abstract, so we can confirm the syndrome-gene association and nothing about the phenotype's details beyond the syndrome's own name.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was the pelvis and uterus involved as well as the limbs?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Roberts syndrome - craniofacial anomalies and TETRAPHOCOMELIA (severe shortening, not absence, of all four limbs), with loss of sister-chromatid cohesion at heterochromatic regions.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: Tetraphocomelia is often described colloquially as 'limbless'. It is mechanistically a cohesion/cell-division disorder, not a limb-patterning one, which is a useful and non-obvious distinction to be able to draw.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Were the limbs absent, or were they present and severely shortened?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Limb agenesis when both are inactivated in the lateral plate mesoderm; a three-deleted-allele hypomorph gives proximal hypoplasia and loss of POSTERIOR skeletal elements.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: A recent (2021) agenesis result, upstream of Tbx and co-regulating Fgf10 enhancers. If the judge's work is on limb INITIATION rather than outgrowth, this is current.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was the phenotype dose-dependent across allele number?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Failure to establish a functional AER and the SHH/FGF loop, with the core limb mesenchyme eliminated by apoptosis; neonatal lethal from absent kidneys plus lung septation defects.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the inhibitor arm of the self-terminating loop and a classic limb-bud gene. Also implicated comparatively: a rapidly evolving GREM1 conserved non-coding element in marine mammals.

welfare.framing: A limbless mouse is a severe phenotype. This section is here because a reviewer will expect it and because its absence would be a hole in the page, not as an apology for the science. The relevant question for a licence or IACUC review is not whether the phenotype is severe - it is - but whether the severity is necessary for the question, and whether a less severe route answers it.

severity_classification.point: European severity classification under Directive 2010/63/EU applies to the BREEDING AND MAINTENANCE of genetically altered lines likely to develop a harmful phenotype, not only to experimental procedures. A line that is limbless at birth is authorised as a harmful-phenotype line before any experiment is performed.
severity_classification.evidence_cite: Zintzsch A et al. 2017, Lab Anim 51:573-582, 'Guidelines on severity assessment and classification of genetically altered mouse and rat lines'
severity_classification.evidence_finding: 'Genetic alterations can unpredictably compromise the wellbeing of animals ... the breeding and maintenance of genetically altered (GA) animals which are likely to develop a harmful phenotype has to be authorized.' The Working Group of Berlin Animal Welfare Officers provides a list of symptoms classified as non-harmful, mild, moderate or severe, with monitoring and refinement strategies and specific housing requirements.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Do not let the animal be born. Analyse at E18.5 by skeletal preparation, at E11.5 by reporter assay, at E10.5 by in-situ hybridisation - which is precisely the protocol Kvon et al. used for everything except the two-week viability photograph. The entire ZRS allelic series was characterised on embryos.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: You learn nothing about postnatal viability, locomotion, growth or welfare - which is exactly the question a 'can you make a limbless mouse' claim turns on.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Use a tissue-restricted conditional (Prx1-Cre) so the lesion does not also remove lungs or kidneys. This both improves the science and removes a large, certain source of suffering that is not even the phenotype of interest.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Breeding complexity; a craniofacial domain in the driver that must be checked.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Use an inducible allele so the lesion is applied in the window that matters. A gene removed after its requirement has passed gives no phenotype at all - Naiche and Papaioannou showed this directly for Tbx4 - so stage selection is a way of asking a sharper question with fewer affected animals.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Tamoxifen effects on pregnancy require vehicle controls.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Take one pair rather than four. A forelimb-only or hindlimb-only animal retains locomotion and is a materially less severe phenotype than tetra-amelia, and for most mechanistic questions it answers the same thing.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: None scientifically, for questions about one limb's network.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Replace with ex vivo limb-bud organ culture, where signalling can be manipulated pharmacologically and lineages tracked longitudinally. Tbx4-null hindlimb buds fail to develop in vitro as they do in vivo, so explants reproduce at least some genetic lesions faithfully.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Animals are still used to source the buds, so this is a refinement and a partial reduction, NOT a replacement, and calling it a replacement would overstate it.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Replace with budoids - mESC-derived organoids containing AER-like, surface-ectoderm and limb-mesoderm cells, undergoing chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking, at >1,000 budoids per differentiation - or with human iPSC-derived PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchyme. These are true replacements and they are scalable.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: The readouts are cell fate, polarisation and cartilage, not a skeleton and not an animal. No dish currently makes a limb; the Underhill/Arostegui methods chapter said in 2021 that no organoid system effectively modelled limb-development complexity, and budoids (2025) are a real advance on that but not a refutation of it.

what_a_licence_or_iacuc_review_would_tur: Is the severe phenotype necessary for the question, or would a one-pair, conditional, or embryonic-only version answer it? For most mechanistic questions the answer is that it would.
Is a non-animal route available for this specific readout? For cell-fate and signalling questions in 2026, increasingly yes; for skeletal and postnatal questions, no.
What is the humane endpoint and who decides it? A limbless neonate cannot right itself, reach a nipple or thermoregulate normally.
What are the housing requirements? The Berlin guidelines pair severity classification with specific housing and monitoring requirements rather than treating classification as a paperwork exercise.

How many animals does the breeding scheme produce for each informative one? A homozygous conditional on two floxed alleles plus a driver is a demanding cross, and reduction is a breeding-design problem as much as an experimental one.

Precedent exists and is documented: the Kvon et al. transgenic and knock-in work was reviewed and approved by the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Animal Welfare and Research Committee, mice were monitored daily and inspected weekly by the committee chair, the head of the facility and veterinary staff, and the facility is AAALAC-accredited. Embryonic samples for in-situ and skeletal preparation were dissected blind to genotype, and knock-in and knock-out experiments used a matched-littermate design.
welfare.our_position: We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm. Nothing on this page was performed by us and no organism, embryo or cell was made by us. The welfare discussion is here because the design space we are describing is one somebody else would have to execute, and a design space presented without its costs is not a design space.

limitations: We ran no experiments. Every route on this page is a reading of someone else's published work, or an explicitly labelled proposal. Nothing here is a result of ours.

ONE source was read at full text (Kvon et al. 2016, via PMC5484524, including figure legends and STAR Methods). Everything else is read at ABSTRACT level, with one exception noted below. No claim on this page is written in the voice of having read a body we did not read.

Summerbell 1974 (PMID 4463222) is cited at LISTING level: the PubMed record resolves and its title and MeSH terms confirm a quantitative AER-excision series in chick, but PubMed holds no abstract for it, so we have read no result statement from that paper and make no quantitative claim from it. The classical premise is restated independently by Lewandoski et al. 2000.

Garavelli et al. 2010 (PMID 21271649, WNT7A / Al-Awadi-Raas-Rothschild) also has no abstract in PubMed. We confirm the syndrome-gene association from the title and MeSH terms and state nothing further about the phenotype.
Every PMID on this page was retrieved from PubMed and resolved to a record during this session; none is quoted from memory or from a secondary summary. DOIs are as returned by PubMed.

SCOPE OF NEGATIVE SEARCHES. All searches were PubMed only, in English, via the pubmed MCP tools. We did not search bioRxiv, medRxiv, patents, theses or non-English sources, and PubMed's query parser ANDs all terms, so a long query returns fewer results than a short one - several of our early searches returned zero for that reason and were repeated with shorter terms. Specific negatives: (1) no molecular mechanism for Lerista limb reduction was found ('Lerista limb reduction skink evolution' returned 4 records, all taxonomic, morphometric or macroevolutionary); (2) no published genetic AER ablation with diphtheria toxin was found ('diphtheria toxin ablation apical ectodermal ridge genetic mouse' returned 4 records, none of them an AER ablation); (3) no auxin-inducible degron study in mouse embryos was found, so the degron route cites dTAG/FKBP work instead; (4) no limb field was found reported in gastruloids or trunk-like structures, searched on PubMed only, which is the wrong place to look first for a 2026 result; (5) no published Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox limb series was found, which is why our own recommendation is labelled 'proposed'; (6) no recombinant-limb experiment using mesenchyme from a defined limb-loss genotype was found. Each of these is an absence in OUR search, not an absence in the literature.

Phenotype statements are quoted or closely paraphrased from the abstracts. Where a paper's own authors flag an inference rather than a measurement - Thewissen et al. on HAND2 association, Sun et al. on cetacean ZRS activity, the 41 Ma and 34 Ma dates - we mark it as theirs and do not restate it as a measurement.

The two published human-to-mouse discordances on this page (Ushiki on CTCF/acheiropodia; Niemann on WNT3 viability) are a standing warning that cross-species transfer of a cis-regulatory or viability claim is unsafe, and we did not systematically check every other route for the same risk.

Two founding Fgf10 papers DISAGREE about whether the limb bud initiates: Min et al. 1998 say initiation was abolished, Sekine et al. 1999 say bud formation initiated but outgrowth did not occur. We preserve the disagreement rather than reconciling it.
Route counts are not evidence counts. 'evidence_strength: proposed' appears on four routes and means exactly what it says: nobody has done it. A design space is not a list of results.

We have never scored a limb enhancer, have no registered calibration anywhere in our system, and have performed no functional validation of any sequence-model output we have produced. Any claim about predicting limb phenotype from sequence is a hypothesis and is labelled as one.
